articles.title: F1 champion Lewis Hamilton visits Gaza border
articles.summary: North Sinai Governor Khaled Megawer briefs the British driver on Egypt-coordinated aid efforts through Rafah crossing.
articles.body:
Seven-time Formula One champion Lewis Hamilton has visited Egypt’s northern El Arish city that borders Gaza to see first-hand efforts to acquire humanitarian aid bound for the Gaza Strip.

North Sinai Governor Khaled Megawer welcomed the British driver on Tuesday and showcased the Egyptian Red Crescent’s aid warehouses.

The governor’s office shared videos on its official Facebook page featuring clips of the visit as Megawer briefed the F1 champion on how relief aid is coordinated.

Hamilton is seen greeting aid workers and inquiring how often they are able to enter Gaza through the Rafah crossing.

Last month , the World Health Organization (WHO) said repeated delays in bringing life-saving medicines, prosthetics and other supplies into Gaza can have “devastating consequences” for Palestinians who urgently need them.

The 41-year-old driver is known to be an advocate for humanitarian and charitable causes.

In 2021, he founded Mission 44, a charity organisation tasked with supporting young people’s access to careers in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM).

In 2022, Hamilton was ranked number five on the Sunday Times Giving List, an annual ranking published by the British newspaper, where he was said to have recently donated 20 million British pounds (about $26m) at the time.

The visit comes after heavy rain and harsh floods overwhelmed Gaza this week, killing at least five people, including four children. Floods have displaced thousands in the process and caused sand embankments to collapse on a displacement camp south of Deir el-Balah.

Gaza’s Civil Defence logged more than 2,100 distress calls by Monday and warned that more than 2,000 buildings are at risk of collapsing.

Israeli strikes have subsequently persisted across the enclave, with at least eight people killed in air attacks on Tuesday , including a father and his 13-year-old son in the Gaza Strip, according to local health sources.

Recent cuts to aid and food assistance have caused the situation to continually worsen as people in Gaza grapple for resources.

articles.title: Flyers' Matvei Michkov Reportedly Eyeing Trade, Latest NHL Rumors amid Contract Year
articles.summary: Matvei Michkov is reportedly ready to part ways with Rick Tocchet and the Philadelphia Flyers.
articles.body:
Matvei Michkov is reportedly ready to part ways with Rick Tocchet and the Philadelphia Flyers.

NHL insider Kevin Weekes reported Tuesday Michkov has a "preference to have a fresh start elsewhere" after the Flyers' 5-10-5 start to the season.

Weekes described Michkov as a "very much in demand potential trade target."

Re-Ranking the Top 2027 NHL Free Agents 📊

The Fourth Period's David Pagnotta and ESPN's Emily Kaplan reported the Flyers hadn't heard from Michkov's camp about a trade request.

Michkov, who is scheduled to hit restricted free agency next summer, currently leads the Flyers with 10 goals in 20 games.

Selected by the Flyers with the seventh pick in the 2023 draft, Michkov made the jump from the KHL to North America ahead of the 2024-25 season.

He scored 26 goals as a rookie, but saw his production decrease after Tocchet was hired as head coach ahead of his sophomore 2026-26 campaign.

Tocchet started out his first season in Philadelphia by switching Michkov from right to left wing and later decreased his ice time. When asked about Michkov's drop in usage last February, Tocchet said the winger "did not come into camp in shape."

Flyers general manager Danny Briere said at the time when asked about Tocchet's comment that Michkov was "going to be here for a long time."

Michkov's standing with the Flyers seemingly improved after the Olympic break, but he was healthy scratched in the playoffs both during his team's first-round series victory over the Pittsburgh Penguins and their second-round sweep by the Carolina Hurricanes.

The Flyers' relationship with Michkov has once more been under scrutiny this season.

Tocchet has tested out splitting up a previously successful duo of Michkov and Martone. Veteran defenseman Nick Seeler accused his teammates of being selfish shortly before having a seemingly heated exchange with Michkov on the bench.

Sean Couturier has called the Flyers "soft" this season. Michkov's reported interest in seeking a trade could be another sign there is locker room discord in Philadelphia just months after the team's trip to the Eastern Conference semifinals.

articles.title: Team USA hero Connor Hellebuyck says that moments beyond online death threats led to his Winnipeg departure
articles.summary: Connor Hellebuyck revealed death threats and off-ice incidents involving his family were among the reasons he requested a trade from the Winnipeg Jets.
articles.body: The New Jersey Devils are in Winnipeg to take on the Jets Tuesday night in what will be goaltender Connor Hellebuyck's return to the city. While he won't start — the team said that despite Hellebuyck's insistence on playing, they went with Jake Allen to avoid a drop in their "expected win probability" — he did face the Winnipeg media. The Team USA hero spent 11 seasons in Winnipeg and won three Vezina Trophies, a Hart Memorial Trophy as league MVP in 2024-25, and led the Jets to a Presidents' Trophy that same season. DEVILS TO SIT STAR GOALIE VS HIS FORMER TEAM OVER 'WIN PROBABILITY,' LEAVING NHL FANS BEWILDERED However, his decision to ask for a trade, followed by him skipping camp and sitting out the start of the season meant that he and the Jets did not part on good terms. Hellebuyck was somewhat mum on his reasons for wanting a trade aside from joining a team he views as a contender, but that changed on Tuesday. TEAM USA HERO CONNOR HELLEBUYCK DISCUSSES THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN PLAYING HOCKEY IN US AND CANADA "I've alluded to this a little bit," Hellebuyck said. "This was a very complex decision, and a very difficult one." Hellebuyck said there was no single moment that led to him wanting out, and that some off-ice issues played into it. "There were some moments and some things that happened to my family that for me crossed the line," he said before adding that he needed to do what was best for his family and his career. He was then asked why the city of Winnipeg was being "pinned" for these things that led to Hellebuyck's decision, when those involved may not have even had a tie to the city. UTAH'S MACKENZIE WEEGAR REACTS TO AMERICAN PLAYERS SEEKING TRADES OUT OF CANADA: 'IT’S A BIT UNFORTUNATE' Hellebuyck strongly rebuffed the idea that he was placing the blame on Winnipeg and its citizens. "There were a few moments that I don’t want to see happen again," Hellebuyck said. "It is more than just online death threats, and I’m gonna ask you to respect my privacy and my family’s privacy; I won’t go deeper than that. TEAM USA STAR BRADY TKACHUK ENDURES 'YOU EAT CRAYONS' TAUNT IN WILD RETURN TO CANADA "But there’s more that made me and my family uncomfortable. On top of some uncertainty with my career, I felt that a change of scenery was best." Hellebuyck might have to face questions again as Tuesday's game is the first of two the Devils and Jets will play over the next few weeks. The 33-year-old from Michigan was a key piece of Team USA's gold medal win at the 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan. articles.title: How P.K. Subban’s luxury lifestyle extends beyond hockey: Exploring his high-end real estate, Beverly Hills villa, interior design choices, media career and philanthropy after the NHL
articles.summary: Dive into the world of P.K. Subban and discover his luxury lifestyle, high-end real estate investments, media career, and philanthropic contributions after his NHL retirement.
articles.body: P.K. Subban built his reputation with an energetic style of play, a standout personality and accomplishments with the Montreal Canadiens, Nashville Predators and New Jersey Devils, and he won the Norris Trophy in 2013 and became one of the most recognizable personalities in hockey, drawing attention for his play, his sense of fashion and his off-ice persona.Subban has continued to build his profile with broadcasting, public appearances and charity initiatives since retiring from professional hockey in 2022. His lifestyle also suggests a love of luxury real estate and well-thought-out interiors. Details of his current real estate portfolio remain private, but his former Beverly Hills residence with Olympian Lindsey Vonn is a documented case of the plush residential style that goes with his public persona.Inside NHL legend P.K. Subban’s luxury lifestyle and real estate investmentsSubban's career in the NHL provided the platform for a lifestyle that combines professional success, travel, fashion and property interests. Across his playing years, he represented the Montreal Canadiens, Nashville Predators and New Jersey Devils, becoming known for his confidence and distinctive personality. His career achievements also helped establish his profile beyond Canadian and American hockey audiences.Real estate became one visible part of that lifestyle. Subban and former fiancée Lindsey Vonn purchased a luxury property in Beverly Hills, California, during their relationship. The home was of interest for its location, architecture and amenities, and for an insight into the residential choices of two high-profile athletes.Inside P.K. Subban’s former Beverly Hills luxury homeOne of the most talked-about properties associated with Subban was the Beverly Hills villa he purchased with Lindsey Vonn in April 2020 for approximately $6.75 million. The former couple later listed the property for $7.175 million following their separation and sold it for $6.9 million in 2021. The transaction attracted attention in the luxury real estate market because of the property's architecture, location and extensive amenities.The Italian-inspired residence covered approximately 5,564 square feet and featured four bedrooms and six bathrooms, and located in the Beverly Hills Post Office area, the property offered privacy, spacious living areas and views of the surrounding canyon landscape.P.K. Subban’s interior style and luxury preferencesSubban's interest in fashion has been a recognizable part of his public personality. He has often been seen in carefully chosen suits, with distinctive accessories and attention to detail. That emphasis on presentation is what provides context to the polished look of the Beverly Hills property.The villa was designed with a mix of traditional architectural features and modern finishes, and neutral interiors, expansive windows and open spaces helped create a bright atmosphere, while marble surfaces and statement features added a sense of luxury.P.K. Subban’s media career and philanthropic workSubban officially announced his retirement from professional hockey on September 20, 2022, ending a 13-season NHL career. He finished with 834 regular-season games, 115 goals and 352 assists, recording 467 points across spells with the Montreal Canadiens, Nashville Predators and New Jersey Devils. His achievements included the 2013 Norris Trophy as the league's top defenseman.Retirement did not mean leaving hockey behind. ESPN signed Subban to a multiyear agreement in November 2022, bringing him into its NHL coverage as an in-studio analyst and occasional in-game contributor. The role gave him an opportunity to use his experience as a former player to discuss team performances, individual players and major league developments.ESPN also said he will host “P.K.’s Places,” a series in which he visits hockey icons and sites of interest in the game’s history. Making the switch to broadcasting allowed him to remain involved with the NHL and develop a new professional identity.Subban’s broadcasting presence also plays off the personality that made him popular in his playing career. His energetic way of communicating, his sense of humor and his willingness to talk about fashion and culture have helped his work stand out against traditional game analysis.Outside of TV, he’s remained active in hockey-related events and projects, all in an effort to grow the game’s audience. As a Toronto-born player who played for Canada internationally, he also has ties to Canadian hockey communities.P.K. Subban’s charitable commitment and community impactPhilanthropy has been one of the most significant parts of Subban's life beyond professional hockey, and in September 2015, he announced a commitment to donate $10 million to the Montreal Children's Hospital through the P.K. Subban Foundation. The pledge was intended to support children and families receiving treatment at the hospitalThat dedication didn’t end when Subban left Montreal for Nashville in 2016. He remained affiliated with the hospital, visiting the young patients and continuing to support the institution. The Nashville Predators documented his visits with teammates, highlighting how the initiative was more than just a financial donation.In a 2023 publication, the Montreal Children’s Hospital Foundation said it had raised $6.3 million to date on the $10 million pledge. This allows for a documented update on the initiative instead of presuming that the entire commitment was already completedSubban also won the NHL's King Clancy Memorial Trophy in 2022 for his leadership and humanitarian work. His foundation has supported underserved youth, youth hockey, racial and social justice initiatives and COVID-19 relief efforts.His philanthropy adds another dimension to his public persona. Beyond hockey, he is interested in luxury property, fashion and broadcasting, and his dedication to the hospital is a sign of how he has given back to communities with his professional success.Life after the NHL P.K. Subban lives in several places. His previous villa in Beverly Hills showed an interest in high-end residential living, and his role at ESPN kept him in touch with the sport that made his name. But the philanthropy, especially the pledge to the Montreal Children’s Hospital, continues to define his legacy off the ice.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Week 10 Fantasy Football Waiver Wire: Corey Kiner, Tank Dell among top pickups
articles.summary: Justin Boone shares his top waiver wire pickups at each position for fantasy football going into Week 10.
articles.body:
Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups.

Roster percentages are generated from Yahoo leagues. Free-Agent Budget (FAB) amounts are based on a $100 salary cap. Only players rostered in less than 50% of leagues are considered.

With Kirk Cousins heading back to Minnesota, the Raiders can finally put their first-overall pick under center. While you're not going to want to use Mendoza against the Seahawks defense this week, his outlook for the rest of the season is quite promising as a highly-drafted pick attached to Klint Kubiak.

The Heisman Trophy winner proved himself to be a good leader in college with excellent on-field awareness and the toughness needed to overcome adversity during games. He has a strong arm to make any throw, but it's his touch passing that stood out. Though Mendoza's not fast enough to be a meaningful runner in the pros, he has enough speed to scramble his way out of trouble and pick up yards on the ground. This all amounts to an intriguing fantasy QB2 with room to grow.

The quarterback position is very picked over at the moment. Malik Willis was featured in this spot last week, but he's now playing through a groin injury that's limited his abilities as a runner and neutered his fantasy potential. So, all that's left are uncomfortable streaming options.

The Steelers are coming off their bye week, which should help the 42-year-old Rodgers (turns 43 in December) feel refreshed for a date with the division rival Bengals.

Rodgers hasn't had many favorable opponents this season, but he did take advantage of his easiest matchup. That just happened to be against the Bengals in Week 3, when the veteran passed for 292 yards and three touchdowns en route to a QB8 finish.

In his last visit to Cincinnati, Rodgers threw four touchdowns back in Week 7 of the 2025 campaign. He's not a slam-dunk streamer, but he's a solid one given the options this week.

Desperation streaming options (if healthy)

Desperation streaming options (if starter is out)

The elite backup RBs who are one injury away from stardom should be rostered everywhere and I'll continue to highlight them in this space until they no longer qualify for this article.

It was clear early in the season that Johnson was one of the best backups to roster, in case anything ever happens to Kenneth Walker III. In recent weeks, Johnson's value has increased even more now that he's offering weekly flex production.

The rookie posted a fluky 128 receiving yards and a score in Week 8, but he followed it up with 34 yards and another touchdown on Sunday. Upcoming matchups with the Falcons, Cardinals and Bills are all spots where Johnson could be a viable flex play while also offering league-winning upside if Walker ever misses time.

Black is in the same situation as Johnson; you can basically just swap Walker's name with Christian McCaffrey's in the previous section.

The 49ers' rookie plays in one of the best offenses in the league and has flashed his potential with at least 60 rushing yards in three of his first eight games, while serving as CMC's direct backup. That includes the past two games, when Black turned 12 touches into 63 yards and a TD against the Falcons, as well as Sunday's outing, which resulted in 11 carries for a season-high 70 yards.

Next up is the Cowboys defense, which is a top-five matchup for fantasy running backs. The 49ers are 4-point favorites in a game with the highest projected point total in Week 10 at 55.5.

Stashing a talented No. 2 back playing behind a 30-year-old starter who handled 450 touches last year is just an obvious move. Black should be rostered everywhere as a flex option with RB1 upside if McCaffrey were ever sidelined.

Rhamondre Stevenson left Sunday's game with a knee injury and was very quickly ruled out. Mike Vrabel didn't have an update Monday morning, but did acknowledge that his back was undergoing an MRI. With TreVeyon Henderson already sidelined indefinitely, that leaves Kiner as the next man up.

Though Kiner hasn't been asked to do much as a pass-catcher, the 2025 UDFA has shown some juice in the run game by topping 50 yards in three of his last five outings in a change-of-pace role.

If Stevenson can't suit up in Week 10, which seems unlikely due to news that he'll probably miss some time, Kiner immediately becomes a high-end fantasy RB3 with the usual touchdown upside that comes with a starter's workload. We can't lock that outcome in, though until we get a proper update on Stevenson's injury.

Josh Jacobs fractured his finger and is set to undergo surgery that will keep him out a maximum of three games.

MarShawn Lloyd missed Week 9 due to a knee injury, which allowed Johnson to step up in Jacobs' absence. Johnson finished with 68 yards and a touchdown, making him the RB11 on the week with just MNF left to be played.

If you're wondering why Johnson isn't higher on this list, just take a look at Green Bay's upcoming schedule. The Packers face the Vikings this week, then have a bye before taking on the Rams.

So, even with Jacobs sidelined, this isn't the ideal setup for a spot starter. On top of that, we aren't sure if/when Lloyd will be available. If Lloyd is active in Week 10, it only further muddies the projections.

If Lloyd remains out, Johnson would be a risky RB3/flex versus the Vikings. If Lloyd plays, then both players would be risky flex options.

With the Saints cutting Kendre Miller, Estimé stepped into a significant role in his first game since joining the Saints. The result was a 47% snap share, which led to 15 carries for 72 yards and a touchdown, as well as another five yards on a catch.

Estimé's presence helped kickstart New Orleans' rushing attack, but his fantasy outlook is directly tied to Travis Etienne Jr.'s health. Etienne, who can be activated off IR at any time, wasn't ready to practice last week. Once we see him back on the field, it will severely diminish Estimé's fantasy value.

However, if Etienne misses another week, fantasy managers will be able to start Estimé as a fringe low-end RB2.

Chris Rodriguez Jr. at TEN (33% rostered)

Sione Vaki vs. NE (Germany) (2% rostered)

Dart-throw flex options (if starter is out)

DeMario Douglas has always been a risky receiver to put in your fantasy lineup due to his low floor. We witnessed that occur in Week 7, when he only delivered three catches for 23 yards.

However, Douglas has posted at least 12 fantasy points in his other four outings over the last five weeks, finishing as a top-10 WR three times. After hauling in five of his nine targets for 102 yards in Week 9, he currently sits as the WR23 with just Monday Night Football remaining.

Four touchdowns during this stretch have helped his cause, but he's come away with very respectable yardage totals in these games with at least 65 in each.

A.J. Brown's recovery timeline remains uncertain and with a bye looming, it seems likely we won't see him until Week 12 at the earliest. Fantasy managers can continue to take advantage by starting Douglas as a WR3/flex option with temporary upside.

Dell's return from a near career-ending injury is one of the best stories in the NFL this season. The fact that he's been productive since getting back on the field only makes it more incredible.

While his 43-yard catch on one target in Week 7 was a bit fluky, it's hard to ignore a nine-target outing this past week. Dell finished the day with four grabs, 105 yards and a score and looked good in the process. However, he still only ran 50% of the routes in a Houston passing attack that's known for rotating receivers behind Nico Collins. We'll need to see more from Dell before we can trust him as an every-week fantasy starter, but he's done enough to warrant being added in most formats as a potential boom-or-bust WR3/flex.

After back-to-back games with at least 50 yards, it was discouraging to see Williams underwhelm with just three catches for 25 yards this week. I'm still holding out hope though.

The rookie continues to play the most snaps and run the most routes in the Commanders' receiver room. This was the third straight outing where Williams accomplished that feat, following Terry McLaurin's season-ending injury.

It's possible Williams levels off as a low-ceiling WR4/flex option for fantasy, but I'm holding for at least another week. The talent is evident and Washington has one of the top-10 easiest schedules for fantasy receivers the rest of the way.

Douglas has played four games this year that weren't impacted by injury. In those contests, the rookie has posted stat lines of 5-94-0, 2-70-2, 4-43-0 and 6-70-0.

With Malik Willis heading to IR, Douglas's fantasy ceiling takes a hit. However, he's still an intriguing rookie who is emerging as the No. 1 target in his offense.

When a first-year player is showing this kind of production early in his career, it's worth taking notice. Even with Kyle McCord under center, Douglas can be started as a WR4/flex given his intriguing matchups against the Colts and Bills the next two weeks.

It's easy to forget, but Bryant had a growing role in the Broncos' passing attack during the opening month before being placed on injured reserve with an ankle injury. In those first four games, Bryant topped 40 yards three times.

So, it was great to see him post a season-high 56 yards and a touchdown on four catches in his first game back since the injury. Jaylen Waddle also suffered a concussion, but he should be cleared after their Week 10 bye.

Regardless, Bryant was a borderline flex option early in the season and has returned with an even better performance. Given Waddle's struggles and Courtland Sutton's age, there's a non-zero chance Bryant becomes the most valuable fantasy receiver in Denver for the rest of the season.

Watkins' fantasy value is difficult to assess because it's entirely dependent on the health of the other receivers in San Francisco.

Keenan Allen was acquired at the trade deadline, but most of the other wideouts on the roster are injured. Deebo Samuel Sr. is nearing a return from a hamstring injury that kept him out for the last month. Mike Evans' Achilles tendinitis is an ongoing problem with no clear recovery timeline. I'll be surprised if he suits up in Week 10. Demarcus Robinson is apparently playing at less than 100%, while De'Zhaun Stribling and Christian Kirk are on IR.

That opened the door for Watkins, who put up four receptions, 86 yards and a touchdown versus the Raiders. That's his second consecutive quality stat line, after a 56-yard performance versus the Falcons prior to the Niners' Week 8 bye.

If everything remains the same with Evans and Deebo sitting out, Watkins will be a boom-or-bust WR4/flex option in a good matchup with the Cowboys this week. However, once Allen is up to speed and the other receivers are healthy, Watkins won't be worth rostering in redraft leagues.

Makai Lemon is 53% rostered but would be the No. 3 WR add behind Tyson and D.Douglas, if available.

In the four games since Terry McLaurin's season-ending injury, Okonkwo has posted stat lines for 4-60-0, 7-69-0, 2-32-0 and 6-57-0.

While he hasn't found the end zone, that type of volume (at least six targets in three of the four appearances) makes him the 10th-most targeted tight end on a per game basis during that stretch.

Okonkwo has moved into the high-end TE2 streamer conversation, with a chance to crack the low-end TE1 range moving forward.

Puka Nacua is heading to IR, Davante Adams is already there and Terrance Ferguson isn't expected back for another couple weeks.

Higbee has disappeared from fantasy relevance following his impressive three-game stretch from Week 3 to Week 5, when he posted 8-62-1, 5-67-0 and 5-83-0. Since then, the veteran has been held to 22 yards or less in four straight contests and hasn't found the end zone.

However, the Rams will have no choice but to increase his targets with Nacua out. That puts Higbee back in the mix as a TE2 streamer with upside.

Eddy Pineiro is 54% rostered but would be the No. 1 K add, if available.

Tyler Bass is 57% rostered but would be the No. 2 K add behind Pinerio, if available.

Quarterbacks: Lamar Jackson, Kyler Murray, Justin Herbert

Running Backs: J.K. Dobbins, Emanuel Wilson

Wide Receivers: Michael Wilson, Xavier Worthy, Chris Godwin Jr., Marvin Harrison Jr., Devaughn Vele

Tight Ends: Mark Andrews, Dalton Schultz

Lamar Jackson is undergoing surgery that will sideline him for 6-10 weeks. If you're stashing him in hopes that he'll return for the fantasy playoffs, you're wasting a roster spot.

Despite the Texans making a trade for Marvin Harrison Jr., he's just part of a big rotation of receivers behind Nico Collins. It's possible MHJ could carve out a bigger role as the season progresses, but it's highly unlikely he'll make a major fantasy impact — unless Collins gets hurt. Even in that scenario, I'm not confident Harrison would step up.

With Jordyn Tyson now in the lineup, Devaughn Vele's days as a fantasy flex option are over.

articles.summary: At the WWE Performance Center, the November 10 edition of WWE NXT needed to set the course of the company going forward after a star-studded show last week.
articles.body:
At the WWE Performance Center, the November 10 edition of WWE NXT needed to set the course of the company going forward after a star-studded show last week.

The winners of the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic, Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno, challenged The Vanity Project for the NXT Tag Team Championships.

Wren Sinclair fought Izzi Dame while Lizzy Rain looked to avenge her loss to Chantel Monroe. John Cena also announced the next invitee to the Cena Classic.

For live grades, reaction and highlights from NXT, check out the recap below.

Shiloh Hill Steps Up to Grayson Waller, and Mason Rook Returns

The show started with CM Punk... or not as Grayson Waller arrives to Punk's music with "Best in the World" on the back of his shirt.

He talked about making the NXT Championship prestigious again then questions if anyone was ready to step up to him.

Shiloh Hill arrived and told Waller that he was the hard worker that the NXT champion was ignoring when he "crapped on" the men's roster.

Waller appreciated Hill's words but told he wasn't ready. As Waller looked to walk away, Mason Rook returned to lay out Waller. Hill caught Waller with a Pop-Up Punch followed by Rook hitting his Running Backpack Cannonball.

It is great to see Rook back after he disappeared from TV with an unknown medical issue. He and Waller already built a clear story for their title match, so it could happen any time.

Hill stepping up to Waller was a nice spot for him, even if he was never going to seriously contend with the NXT champion on the microphone.

Waller played nice for now, and he let Hill look like a threat. If NXT leans into him as the true workhorse of the division, he could genuinely be the man to take down Waller.

After last week was more about the big names in attendance, this was a great way to immediately put the focus back on multiple rising names in NXT.

The show started with a recap from last week.

Wade Barrett joined Vic Joseph on commentary for the night.

In a non-PG reference, Waller said that Tony D'Angelo was on a bridge with cement shoes after his loss to the NXT champion.

Waller referenced the Pipebomb as he called himself the true Best in the World.

Hill talked up why he is the workhorse of the men's division, helping with every live event and working more matches than anybody in the NXT roster.

Last Time in Action: EK Prosper lost to North American champion Jackson Drake due to the interference of Kam Hendrix (NXT, October 27); Hendrix lost to Mason Rook (NXT, September 1).

EK Prosper shocked Kam Hendrix early with explosive offense. Prosper caught Hendrix with a strong Blockbuster, but Hendrix responded with a Rebound Clothesline.

The two fought to the outside where Prosper caught Hendrix with a Springboard Moonsault off the apron to the floor into the commercial break.

Hendrix took over out of the break, laying into Prosper. Prosper fired back with a Tornado DDT, a series of Clotheslines then a Springboard Moonsault into a near-fall.

Prosper went for another Springboard Moonsault, and Hendrix caught him with a Showtime Kick for a close near-fall.

Hendrix knocked Prosper off the top rope into Fireman's Carry Slam for another near-fall. Prosper ducked Hendrix who bounced face-first off the top turnbuckle.

Prosper finished the match with a Moonsault. Afterward, Hendrix ripped apart the ringside area in frustration until an official intervened.

Explosive offense was the name of the game for both men in this, but the timing was awkward. It was obvious especially that Hendrix was rushing to his spots.

Whenever Showtime is in control, he is less focused on building the story and psychology of the match and more on looking cool or silly.

That is expected with a less experienced wrestler, and Hendrix has obvious athleticism to spare. However, he has not shown obvious growth yet.

Prosper is noticeably more experienced, though his struggle is more on the character side than the in-ring. He can delivered against anyone, but he does not have the natural charisma of, say, a Je'Von Evans despite a similar style.

In the ring, to take the next step forward, Prosper does need more move variety as he relies so heavily on the Moonsault and could use more established signature offense.

Both men got short promo spots before the break to sell why they would win. This is a great idea to get more talent promo time each week.

Vic Joseph highlighted footage from Halloween Havoc where Prosper attacked Hendrix. Vic and Wade Barrett agreed Prosper needed to stand up for himself.

Earlier in the day in the locker room, John Cena invited Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno to the Cena Classic.

After watching the video, The Vanity Project complained about their challengers getting the invite instead of them. Myka Lockwood told them to do something about it.

The Vanity Project found Noam and Romeo backstage and laid them out.

Last Time in Action: Wren Sinclair lost to Kelani Jordan for the NXT Women's Championship, and Izzi Dame defeated Zaria (NXT Halloween Havoc, October 31).

Izzi tried to bully Wren early, but she struggled against the technical precision of his opponent. Izzi avoided the Final Wrench early, but Wren knocked her on the floor with a Dropkick off the apron into the commercial break.

During the break, Izzi sent Wren into the steel post and Suplexed her on the floor. Izzi dived into another Dropkick from Wren right out of the break.

After exchanging strikes, Wren caught a running Izzi with a Butterfly Suplex for two. Izzi fired back with a Chokeslam for a near-fall.

Wren caught Izzi in the Final Wrench, but Izzi rolled free. Wren ducked a Big Boot and lifted Izzi for a Spinning Alabama Slam, but her back gave out.

Izzi responded with a Running Knee for the win. Immediately after the bell, Zaria Speared and F5ed Izzi to stand tall.

The dynamics in this match worked better than most recent Izzi matches as the technical style worked better with Izzi's measured pace.

The two hit their spots well and flowed significantly better than Izzi and Zaria had at Halloween Havoc, even if that is the actual story NXT is selling.

It is odd that Wren is immediately taking losses after she was elevating to the main event scene, but commentary tried to protect her by selling she was still hurting from Halloween Havoc.

This booking indicates that there are no immediate plans for Wren to stay in title contention, though her work in this match shows she is a valuable veteran for the less experienced and more awkward wrestlers in NXT.

Wren-QCC chants were the most focused crowd reaction so far of the night.

Both women sold a specific body part. Wren focused on her back while Izzi struggled with her hand due to the Final Wrench early.

Myles Borne mocked Tony D'Angelo standing on a bridge in the dark, but Tony D told he was done thinking and was headed back to work.

articles.title: 'That was just a lie': Malik Nabers slams Fox broadcasters' body language comments
articles.summary: Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers isn’t done responding to comments from Fox’s Joe Davis and Greg Olsen about his body language during New York’s 19-11 win o...
articles.body:
Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers isn't done responding to comments from Fox's Joe Davis and Greg Olsen about his body language during New York's 19-11 win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday.

During the game, the Fox NFL broadcast zeroed in on Nabers' body language several times, including after he was seen slamming his helmet following a frustrating fourth-quarter sequence.

"His body language has been terrible today," Davis said at one point .

"I have played with a lot of really good wide receivers, a lot really good players. There's never been a great wide receiver who hasn't demanded the ball. That kind of comes with the territory," Olsen said of Nabers. "But there is a very fine line between being demanding, being a competitor, and all those great things. That's great. It just can never cross that it feels like it takes away from the success of your teammates. So when your teammate catches a wide-open touchdown, you need to be the happiest guy on the field. You can't still be worried about your targets. That's the fine line. He is a talented, young, really good player. You've just got to keep it in check."

The Giants won the game, but Davis and Olsen's commentary about Nabers became all anyone wanted to talk about afterward, including the wide receiver, who slammed the Fox commentators on social media .

"Y'all be trying create a narrative on me soo bad it's actually crazy!!" Nabers wrote Sunday night. "If you [don't] like the way I play the game keep the camera off me!! SIMPLE!

"But @gregolsen88 callin me a bad teammate when every team I've been on, there's NOBODY I've played with had said dat bout me is crazy! My face the same way if I'm havin a good game, bad, winning or losing. If it's a problem 1. Keep the camera off me. 2. Pray bout it! Simple."

Several New York radio hosts pushed back on Davis and Olsen , and the New York Post wrote a story that initially misattributed quotes to Olsen about Nabers. That prompted a response from Olsen, who shared his comments on X , writing, "At no point did we ever say he was a bad teammate."

All of which brings us to Tuesday, when Nabers met with the media before Thursday's game against the Washington Commanders.

Nabers told reporters that the Fox broadcast tried to "create a narrative" about him that simply isn't true.

"I just feel like the narrative on me is always all the bad body language things that people have been saying about me," Nabers said . "But as far as that, if it's a problem with anybody, the cameras can stay off me. The thing about it is, don't tell the world something that's not me. I'm gonna speak up for myself all the time because there's nobody else that's going to be able to speak up for me. So, I'm going to use my own voice and be able to speak up about me being a bad teammate. And I felt like that was just a lie, just attacking my character as a football player and as a teammate. Like I said, I've never been on a team where anyone has called me a bad teammate that I know of."

"I felt like after the game, when I got the opportunity to hear those things, I had to speak up about that because those things are just not true," he continued. And as far as just the bad body language thing, everybody's always talking about my body language. Like I've said, my body language is the same all the time. Whether I'm having a good game, bad game, losing, winning. You can go to games, and you can see it for yourself if you want to go look. But as far as the bad body language and things being said that I was saying on the sideline – especially from people that's watching the game, they don't know what's going on down on the field. So, you don't know what is being said, you don't know if I'm mad, you don't know if I'm not.

That's just really everything on it; my body language is the same all the time. My facial expression is the same all the time. I think a lot of people just don't know that because they don't know me."

Nabers was asked if he's spoken with Olsen since, saying that he hasn't, but "he can reach out, and we can have a simple conversation."

It's an interesting predicament for Olsen, who hasn't really been in a situation like this before as a broadcaster. All eyes are on the highly rated and sought-after NFL analyst to see if he offers a clarification or reaches out to Nabers this week, and how he reacts to his comments touching a nerve with a player.

articles.title: Mile posts: Items on Grace Steinmetz, Aaron Fynaardt, Kaitlyn Knoche, Bryant Keller, Addison Liston, Lance Sobaski
articles.summary: Since arriving on at Bellevue, Grace Steinmetz has competed in eight Frontier Conference races and has won seven.
articles.body:
Grace Steinmetz rarely loses when she steps into Frontier Conference competition.

The Heartland Christian High School graduate from Council Bluffs captured her seventh league title in Billings, Montana, on Friday, Nov. 6. The Bellevue (NE) University sophomore steamed to victory in the conference's cross country championships at Amend Park. Steinmetz covered the 6K (3.7 miles) course in 21:12.6, a 5:42.1 pace per mile, to win by nearly 40 seconds.

"We expected Grace to repeat and thought (teammate) Maggie (Boley) had a very good chance of qualifying, too, and they both delivered. It's exciting to have both women at nationals, and both are in the All-American conversation."

Steinmetz leads off this edition of the WEEKEND UPDATE of the best performances by Iowa-based collegiate and post collegiate distance runners and triathletes.

Steinmetz helped drive the Bruins to an unexpected runner-up team finish with 109 points, 70 behind Carroll (MT).

Since arriving on the Bellevue, Nebraska, campus, Steinmetz has competed in eight Frontier Conference races and has won seven (2025 cross country; 2026 indoor mile, 3,000, 5,000; 2026 outdoor 5,000, 10,000). Her only loss was in the 1,500 final outdoors, when she was second.

Will return to the Frontier Conference men's race in a bit, but switching to the Gulf South Conference cross country meet in Hermitage, Tennessee, on Nov. 6. Union (TN) senior Aaron Fynaardt, who prepped at Des Moines Christian, picked up fifth overall in the 8K race in a new personal record of 23:59.4. Fynaardt moved up three spots from a year ago while pacing Union to fifth in the team race with 137 points. Lee (TN) won the team crown with 16 points and Lee freshman Kylian Boulanger as the champion in 23:30.2.

St. Ambrose senior Kaitlyn Knoche fared well in her first Heart of America Conference race. The North Scott product took second in the league meet at Baldwin City, Kansas, on Nov. 7 in a new PR of 22:00.2 for 6K. Knoche ended up just 4.9 seconds behind Central Methodist junior Sarah Kirby. The Bees, sixth in the team race, were competing in their first Heart of America league meet since leaving the Chicagoland Collegiate Athletic Conference in May. Knoche won four CCAC individual titles.

The Mount Mercy women finished second in the team race behind the strength of two Iowans. Senior Abby Knepper, a Beckman (Dyersville) grad, took fourth in 22:17.0. She was the reigning Heart of America champion. Fellow senior Kalin Rotzoll, who competed for Clear Creek-Amana, was sixth in 22:22.1.

The leader for 10th-place William Penn was sophomore and former Central Springs (Manly) athlete Claire Rye in 10th in 22:51.1. Like Knoche, Knepper and Rotzoll, Rye qualified for nationals with her finish. The No. 3 runner for Mount Mercy, which scored 77 points, was junior Lourdes Mason. The former Mount Vernon-Lisbon prep ran a new best of 23:00.7 for 12th at the Mike Spielman Cross Country Course.Benedictine (KS) took the team title with 49 points.

In the men's 8K competition, ex-Anamosa competitor Jack Stamp narrowly missed a PR after achieving first-team all-conference honors in ninth place. The Mount Mercy sophomore was timed in 25:27.3. Sophomore teammate Noah Gregoire, a Liberty High grad, ran 25:37.4 for 11th. Another Mustang, freshman Owen Miller, took 15th in 25:51.1 to help Mount Mercy place fourth in the team race with 98 points. Miller competed for Cedar Rapids Prairie.

William Penn was one spot back of Mount Mercy and pacing the Statemen was senior and former Dallas Center-Grimes athlete Carson Springer in 28th. Springer ran 26:55.2. The leader for sixth-place Grand View University was senior Matthew Bonner, who attended Des Moines Roosevelt. Bonner ran 26:58.7 for 29th. Sophomore teammate Damion Winkler, an Ames High product, ran 27:05.5 for 32nd. Seth Countryman, another Mount Mercy sophomore who ran for Anamosa, was 33rd in 27:05.7. One spot behind him was William Penn senior and ex-Pleasant Valley prep Andrew Miller in 27:06.6.

Park U. won the team title with 21 points and Park sophomore Isaac Rivera was the champion in 24:58.9.

Two Iowans led the Augustana University men to the team title at the NSIC championships in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, on Nov. 7. Redshirt sophomore Bryant Keller, a four-time NSIC individual champion in indoor and outdoor track, covered the 8K course in 24:20.5 for third place and first-team all-league honors. Keller is a Glenwood grad. Freshman teammate Emerson Vokes, who attended Grundy Center, took 12th in 24:52.7 as the Vikings scored 25 points to top Minnesota State by 43 points. Mavericks sophomore Jonathan Owen ran 26:03.6 for 45th place for Minnesota State. Owen is a Valley High product. Wayne State (NE) sophomore Matt Richardson, a former Baxter competitor, ran 27:00.5 for 81st. Minnesota State sophomore Luis Pfister was the winner in 24:09.4.

In the women's 6K competition, Winona State sophomore Emily Meyer picked up 18th overall in a new PR of 21:44.1 as Winona won the team crown with 45 points. Meyer, the No. 4 runner, attended Cedar Falls. Her teammate, junior Stella Rusch, took the individual title in 19:51.6.

The top-ranked (by the U.S. Track and Field and Cross Country Coaches Association) Dordt University women steamrolled to their seventh consecutive team title at the Great Plains Athletic Conference meet on its home course Nov. 7. The Defenders scored a perfect 15 points to leave St. Mary (NE) far behind by 70 points.

Running second overall behind champion Joy Koole (21:11.2) for the 6K distance was sophomore Addison Liston. The Unity Christian (Orange City) product ran a new best of 21:18.5 to pick up first-team all-league honors in Sioux Center. She was third a year ago. Finishing in the top 15, but not scoring for Dordt was freshman Katie Young, another Unity grad, ran a new PR of 22:14.2 for ninth. Senior teammate Isabella Webb was 12th in 22:33.5. Webb picked up her fourth top-15 GPAC finish. She attended Waukee High.

Jumping in front of them and breaking up the Dordt juggernaut was Northwestern College senior Emily De Groot. The former MOC-FV (Orange City) runner was timed in 21:54.9 for sixth place. Fellow Red Raiders senior Kayden Spencer, who prepped at Ogden, was 13th in a new PR of 22:35.2 to help Northwestern secure fourth in the team race with 107 points.

Morningside University took fifth in the team race with 131 points and sophomore Estefana Beisswenger was the leader in 14th place. The Cherokee Washington product ran a new best of 22:35.5 for 14th. Junior teammate Gabby Ryan, who competed for Sergeant Bluff-Luton, was 18th in a new PR of 22:45.1. Dordt sophomore Elyse Zwart was 23rd in 22:54.1. Zwart attended Boyden-Hull. Morningside freshman Silvia Kampbell was the Mustangs' No. 3 runner in 24th place in 22:55.2. Northwestern freshman Teagan Tracy, a former MOC-FV runner, was 26th in 23:02.2. Concordia (NE) freshman Amanda Smith cracked the top 30 with a 29th-place effort in 23:10.4. Smith ran for Earlham.

The Dordt men won their competition, but by a far smaller margin than the Defender women, 45-62, over Doane. Running third for the Defenders and taking ninth overall was senior Caleb Van Beek in a new best of 25:13.3 for 8K. Van Beek is a Western Christian (Hull) grad. Concordia finished a solid third with 69 points and senior Aidan Limback crossed second for his team in a new best of 25:19.4. Limback graduated from Valley.

Dordt freshman Tyler Rozenboom cracked the top 15 in his first GPAC team by taking 15th in a new best of 25:30.3. Rozeboom competed for Unity Christian. The next finisher was Dordt junior and ex-Le Mars Community prep Trace Obbink in 25:30.7. He was followed by former Dowling Catholic athlete Brett Gifford, now a junior at Dordt. Gifford ran a new best of 25:36.4.

Northwestern College secured fourth place with 92 points and junior Alik McIlravy picked up 20th place. The North Polk product ran a new best of 25:53.7 as the Red Raiders' No. 3 runner. Freshman teammate Davis Johnson, the No. 4 finisher for Northwestern, took 24th in 26:00.6. Mount Marty junior Joseph Cross was the champion in 24:29.0.

Switching to the roads and the Boston Half Marathon in Massachusetts on Nov. 8. Placing eighth overall in the men's professional competition was 2021 Iowa State NCAA indoor 5,000 champion Wesley Kiptoo in 1:03:03. He is a HOKA Naz Elite athlete based in Bellemont, Arizona. The winner was Habtom Samuel of Eritrea in 59:49.

Seven-time Loras College NCAA champion Kassie Parker, aiming to win the USATF Running Circuit season-long title in the California International Marathon in Sacramento next month, jumped into the women's half marathon and finished ninth in 1:11:10. The Crown Running athlete who ran for Clayton Ridge (Guttenberg) was 1:56 behind winner Fentaye Belayneh of Ethiopia. Parker was the third-best American.

"I knew what time I wanted to run and went for it," Parker wrote on Instagram. "Felt strong until my legs couldn't push up the lengthy hills. Marathon training is rough and I didn't exactly taper for this race as it's my main goal."

Moving to the CNO Financial Indianapolis Monumental Marathon on Nov. 7, where recent Wartburg College 3,000 steeplechase national runner-up Lance Sobaski, 22, picked up the victory in the 5K. The Washington High grad who is now with the Driftless Distance Project squad ran 14:29, a 4:39 average, to win by six seconds.

Finishing third in the women's competition was new Driftless teammate Peyton Steffen, who also took runner-up nationally in the 3,000 steeplechase in May. The ex-Marion and Central College competitor, 23, ran 16:57. The winner was Rebecca Schmitt, 34, in 15:57.

In the women's half marathon, former Ballard (Huxley) prep Abby Kohut-Jackson finished 24th in that competition and 157th overall in 1:15:56, a 5:48 pace per mile. Kohut-Jackson, 28, now resides in St. Louis. The winner was Mikayla Reed, 26, in 1:08:49.

In the men's half marathon, Running Wild Elite's Max Murphy, 24, of Bettendorf placed 20th overall in 1:04:58. Murphy is a Pleasant Valley grad who competed for Iowa before finishing at North Carolina. RWE men's team coordinator Devin Allbaugh was 35th overall in 1:06:40. Allbaugh, 36, is also a Pleasant Valley product who lives in Bettendorf. Anthony Carney Jr., another Driftless squad member who ran for the University of Dubuque, secured 77th among the men in 1:10:39. Carney Jr., 22, lives in Lake Geneva, Wisconsin. Will Lusty, a former Runablaze athlete now living in Chicago, was 82nd in 1:11:19. Lusty is 26. RWE's Aidan Armstrong, who competed for Muscatine and North Central (IL), ran 1:12:37 for 89th. Armstrong, 23, lives in Muscatine. The winner was Owen Smith, 23, in 1:01:39.

In the featured marathon, former Unity Christian and Dordt standout Jacob Vander Plaatts easily set a new best of 2:18:45, a 5:18 pace per mile, while taking 26th overall. Vander Platts, 27, resides in Sioux Center. RWE's Steve Froeschle, 32, of Davenport grabbed 44th overall in 2:23:28. He competed for Davenport Assumption and St. Ambrose. His brother, Dan, was 49th in 2:24:06. Dan, 36, also attended Assumption and resides in Davenport. Fitness Sports Distance Project runner Ethan Mesenbrink, an ex-Gilbert prep, ran 2:26:31 for 74th. Mesenbrink, 25, lives in Ames. The winner was Johnnie Guy, 32, in 2:11:45.

In the women's competition, Runablaze Iowa's Melanie Hamilt crushed her previous best by about five minutes while claiming 30th in 2:42:19, a 6:12 pace per mile. Hamilt, 31, lives in Iowa City. FSDP's Gabby Skopec, 27, of Coralville was 53rd in that competition in 2:48:28. Skopec ran for Iowa City West and Iowa.

A strong field also assembled for the Good Life Halfsy Half Marathon in Lincoln, Nebraska, on Nov. 8. Placing fourth overall was former Morningside standout Garret Ehlers, 35, of Sioux City in 1:06:19. Placing sixth was Runablaze's Tyler Lance, 31, of Algona in 1:07:41. Former Runablaze athlete Jay Welp, a 34-year-old now based in Cedar Falls, was next to finish in 1:07:28. Eein McKinley, who competed at West Monona and Morningside, came in 14th in 1:11:56. McKinley, 21, lives in Sioux City. The winner was Ryder Searle, 30, of Denver in 1:05:16.

Placing third overall among the women and the top female 40 and over was Runablaze's Pasca Cheruiyot. The Ankeny woman, 40, ran 1:17:56.

At the 13th annual Hillbilly Hike races from Indianola to Carlisle on Nov. 7, Runablaze's Tyson Wieland took the half marathon victory in 1:09:05. Wieland, 32, of Des Moines ran for Johnston in high school. He held off former Simpson College and Urbandale competitor Cole Leggett, 23, by 42 seconds.

The women's half marathon champion was ex-Valley High product Lauren (Schulze) Wood, 24, of the Runablaze squad. Wood ran 1:22:23. Emily Wood, 31, of Saint Charles was runner-up in 1:24:27. Wieland's wife, Elise, was third in 1:24:39. Elise Wieland, 27, competed for Southeast Warren and Simpson College.

The women's 5K champion was Runablaze's Susie Duke of rural Searsboro. Duke, 46, was timed in 17:58.

Shifting back to college conference meets and the GLVC Championships in Springfield, Missouri on Nov. 7, where Truman State junior Clare Stahr picked up 14th overall in the women's 6K race in 21:33.5. The ex-Gilbert athlete ran a new best while finishing as the No. 1 runner for the third-place Bulldogs (106 points) at the Allison Sport Complex. Lewis took the team title with 53 points and Rockhurst sophomore Carrington Hessen was the winner in 20:01.9.

Moving back to the Frontier Conference, where Bellevue senior Robert Siford was the No. 7 finisher for the Bruins in 36th place. The Council Bluffs Abraham Lincoln grad covered the 8K course in 27:27.0. Bellevue was second in the team race with 65 points, 26 behind Rocky Mountain.

articles.title: Lakers Shake Up Roster, Bring in New Center Amid Frontcourt Depth Concerns
articles.summary: The Lakers shuffled the fringes of their roster, moving out center Lawson Lovering, who was taking a two-way spot, in favor of center Carson Cooper. The post...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers shuffled the fringes of their roster, moving out center Lawson Lovering, who was taking a two-way spot, in favor of center Carson Cooper.

The Lakers signed Cooper to a two-way contract after he appeared in one game for the Memphis Grizzlies before being waived.

Cooper was on a two-way deal with Memphis, and now he joins the Lakers on the same deal.

He spent four years in college, finishing off his career with a senior year at Michigan State, where he averaged averaging 11.1 points on 58.4% shooting, 7.1 rebounds, 1.5 assists, and 1.0 blocks in 26.8 minutes.

Lovering, meanwhile, inked a two-way deal in late October, with the Lakers hoping the big man would show something as a backup center.

However, he just got garbage time run with LA, appearing in two games.

Why the Lakers really need a back-up center

Right now, the Lakers have Walker Kessler taking most of the minutes at center, averaging 30+ minutes per game, with the rest going to either Sandro Mamukelashvili or Jarred Vanderbilt at the small-ball five.

Against teams without two standout big men, the Lakers can succeed in those matchups.

However, if Kessler is off the floor and a big body is on the floor, it is tough for the Lakers to survive in certain matchups.

If the Lakers don't find one via trade or the buyout market, they'll need to hope they hit on one of these two-way players. Lovering failed to stick, but head coach JJ Redick will hope Cooper can help ease the need for a big man.

Luka Doncic really thrives with a quality big man, and he can make them play better than their actual level because he makes the game easy for them.

Cooper doesn't have a high bar to clear, and if he stays around, his game can really come together.

articles.title: Thomas Haugh records double-double as Florida defeats Florida St. for 6th straight time, 81-72
articles.summary: (AP) — Thomas Haugh had 21 points and 10 rebounds as No. 1 Florida defeated Florida State 81-72 on Tuesday.
articles.body:
TALLAHASSEE, Fla. (AP) — Thomas Haugh had 21 points and 10 rebounds as No. 1 Florida defeated Florida State 81-72 on Tuesday.

Haugh made 3 of 6 shots from beyond the arc and 10 of 12 from the free-throw line as he recorded his second double-double of his senior season.

Alex Condon added eight points and 10 rebounds as the Gators (3-0), who out rebounded FSU 41-29 and won their the sixth straight game in the series.

Sebastian Rancik had 17 of his 23 points in the second half for Florida State (2-1). Rancik shot 8 of 17 from the floor but he was just 1 of 7 from 3-point range.

Anthony Robinson added 19 points on 6-of-12 shooting.

Florida shot 41.2% (21 of 51) from the floor and 30 of 41 (73.2%) from the free-throw line.

Florida was able to maintain the lead because of its rebounding edge and perimeter defense. The Gators held the Seminoles to just 4 of 21 (19%) from 3-point range, with Robinson drilling a pair of shots from long range in the final minutes in a furious attempt to close the gap.

Florida State shot 27 of 62 (43.5%) overall and 14 of 18 (77.8%) from the free-throw line.

Haugh had seven points and six rebounds in the first half as Florida held a 31-29 lead the half. The Gators were 6 of 19 from 3-point range in the first 20 minutes as the Seminoles went 0 for 9 from behind the arc.

Florida State: Hosts Texas A&M-Corpus Christi on Friday.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown's pregame interaction with Jayson Tatum was ice cold
articles.summary: It sure seems like Jaylen Brown wasn't happy to see Jayson Tatum before 76ers vs. Celtics.
articles.body:
Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum played a bunch of years together for the Boston Celtics, winning a title together. But then Brown got sent to the Philadelphia 76ers amid so many questions about his relationship with Tatum that haven't really been answered.

With all eyes on the Celtics and Sixers game on Tuesday night between Brown and Tatum, would we see a little love between the two former teammates? The answer is, it seems, no. As Tatum came over and Brown spun the ball on his finger, Tatum put his hand on Brown in an awkward dap. Brown didn't do... well, anything back.

Is that proof that Brown doesn't like Tatum? His way of saying that they're on different teams and it's time compete? Maybe we'll find out after the game.

Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum have talked about their alleged beef

Tatum said a couple of weeks ago that "There's no animosity. There's no beef." Brown, meanwhile, said there was "nothing" for them to talk about .

articles.title: Rutgers basketball, Lino Mark light up NJIT for 101 points
articles.summary: 5 takeaways as the Scarlet Knights improved to 2-0 in impressive fashion
articles.body:
PISCATAWAY – It took Lino Mark about three seconds to go coast-to-coast for a layup Tuesday, weaving around defenders like they were standing still.

Rutgers basketball's much-improved sophomore guard put on a high-octane show against NJIT, leading the Scarlet Knights' 101-64 romp and entertaining the crowd of about 3,500 at Jersey Mike's Arena.

Mark tallied 17 points, seven rebounds and four assists while committing no turnovers in 21 minutes. He shot 5-of-9 from the floor and 7-of-9 from the free-throw line. His rebounding was as impressive as his ball-handling – at 6-foot-2 and 180 pounds, he's one of the smallest players on the court.

Rutgers (2-0) also got 17 points and six assist from senior guard Tariq Francis against his old program. The Scarlet Knights committed just six turnovers – a mere three before garbage time.

NJIT (1-2), which is a contender to win the America East Conference, was led by sophomore guard David Bolden (18 points, 3 assists).

For the second straight game, acting head coach Brandin Knight called on freshman center Mervedi Miteo and freshman wing Diego Garavaglia early.

Miteo checked in during the first timeout, replacing starting postman Christian Gurdak even though he was foul-less. The 6-foot-10, 270-pound Congo native, who played high school ball in Spain, attacked the boards like a beast (five rebounds, including three offensive boards, in 13 minutes). He also blocked two shots.

Miteo is only 17 years old but he already has a Big Ten frame and knows how to position it. Once he finds a finishing touch, look out.

Garavaglia, a 6-foot-7 Italian import, drilled a 3-pointer on the fast break, taking a pass from Francis and swishing it in stride from the right wing. He also grabbed four boards in 12 minutes.

Knight shortened his main rotation to 11 guys but did add sophomore guard Kaden Powers, who missed the New Haven game due to illness. Sophomore forward Will Sydnor was relegated to garbage time late in the second half but made the most of it, tallying 10 points in just six minutes.

The 6-foot-8 transfer from Manhattan, who was sidelined all summer and early fall with a high ankle sprain, made brief appearances in the exhibition against St. John's and the opener against New Haven and didn't produce much either time.

Sydnor's progress is notable because after averaging 13.9 points and 6.8 rebounds as a freshman at Manhattan, he was projected to fill a big role in the Scarlet Knights' somewhat thin frontcourt.

After drawing a charge in the opener, the junior walk-on grabbed a rebound, got fouled and made two free throws in the final minute. That provoked the biggest roar of the night from the student section. Fradkin is the program's lone walk-on and a holdover from last season.

The Highlanders were 48 hours removed from beating Saint Peter's on a halfcourt buzzer-beater by redshirt freshman guard Brandon Stores, and after Rutgers will board a bus and head south to Richmond for a Wednesday night game at Atlantic 10 powerhouse VCU.

You read that correctly – NJIT has back-to-back nights on the road, 300 miles apart. That's just about unheard of, but it's the only windows those games could be scheduled and that's valuable revenue for the Highlanders. It's buy-game living, on steroids.

The warm-up portion of Rutgers' schedule concludes with a visit from Bryant (1-2) Friday at 6 p.m. Bryant was picked to finish fifth the America East Conference's preseason poll – one spot behind NJIT. Then it gets real with a trip to Las Vegas and a date with eighth-ranked Houston.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown appears to blow off Jayson Tatum's greeting before Celtics-76ers
articles.summary: In Jaylen Brown's first game against the Celtics, he seemingly ignored a quick greeting from former teammate Jayson Tatum.
articles.body:
Their first interaction as opponents was very brief — if not entirely cold or indifferent.

In Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown's first game against the Boston Celtics , he seemingly ignored a quick greeting from former teammate Jayson Tatum, with whom he played for nine seasons.

The relationship between Brown and Tatum has cooled after the Celtics opted to move on from Brown, culminating in the July trade that sent Brown to the Sixers .

The two have talked publicly about their relationship and have indicated that they have not communicated since the deal.

During the moments right before tip-off Tuesday, Nov. 10, Tatum approached Brown and tapped Brown once on the right arm and twice on his chest as he walked past him. Brown, who was spinning the basketball on his finger, barely acknowledged Tatum and did not reciprocate the greeting.

As soon as the game tipped off, Brown was matched up guarding Tatum, and Tatum eventually forced Brown into a turnover on the other end when he swatted the ball off Brown's leg; there was significant contact on the play, but Tatum was not called for a foul.

Seconds later, after Brown had argued with officials, he committed a foul on Tatum.

articles.title: A lockout is coming and the Dodgers don't care
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS — Brandon Gomes tried to watch the World Series.
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS — Brandon Gomes tried to watch the World Series. He made it through a couple of games.

"I tried to watch the first couple games, and then after that, I was like, this is personally too painful," the Dodgers general manager said Tuesday at the GM meetings. "I think I'll just check the box score afterwards."

It's hard to blame him. The Dodgers were trying to become the first team in a quarter-century to win three straight World Series titles. Instead, the Milwaukee Brewers swept them in the National League Championship Series, a year after the Dodgers had swept Milwaukee in the same round and then beat Tampa Bay for the first championship in franchise history.

Asked whether it took any sting away that the team that knocked them out went on to win it all, Gomes didn't hesitate.

"No, it doesn't take any sting away," he said. "You just don't feel good if you don't win."

That's the part of the Dodgers that should worry the rest of baseball. Two championships didn't make losing any easier for them. If anything, it made it worse. And while most of the sport spent this week in Las Vegas bracing for a lockout when the collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1, the Dodgers sounded like a team that hasn't changed a thing.

"For us, we're totally focused, business as usual," Gomes said, "Trying to make sure we're as prepared as possible in case things happen in different ways, whether that's a trade or free agency."

That's not a slogan. It's how the Dodgers have operated since Guggenheim bought the team, and nothing about a work stoppage or a salary cap proposal is going to change it.

Gomes was asked about salary cap proposals that would put the Dodgers well over the line before they sign a single new player. He shrugged it off.

"I think the biggest thing is we're going to function like we always do," Gomes said, "and whatever it is, it is, and we'll figure it out."

Asked for his best guess on when opening day will be, he laughed.

"I don't even know what opening day schedule is right now," he said.

Every other front office in Las Vegas is trying to figure out how to plan for a season that may not start on time under rules that don't exist yet. The Dodgers are planning to be the best team in baseball whenever it starts, and the oddsmakers agree. Even after Milwaukee's 103-win season and championship, the sportsbooks in Las Vegas opened the Dodgers as the 2027 World Series favorite at +310, ahead of the Brewers at +500.

The easy narrative after a sweep is that the Dodgers got old. Gomes isn't buying it.

"Worry? No. Are we cognizant of it? Sure," he said when asked about the age of his roster. "We certainly had a team capable of winning the World Series, and my assumption is had we won, everybody would be saying, 'You have to run that team back.'"

He's right. The same core that couldn't hit in October is the core that won the previous two Octobers. Gomes said the Dodgers "really like our core" and believe it can "be a championship caliber team" again. He also said the front office "certainly" doesn't feel compelled to trade from it.

That doesn't mean they'll stand still. They never do. Tarik Skubal is a free agent, and Gomes left no doubt about how the Dodgers feel about him. "We know we love the player," he said. "We love the human." If Skubal doesn't return, Gomes pointed to Roki Sasaki's second half, Emmet Sheehan and a healthy Gavin Stone, and he named the Brewers as proof that a team can cover innings without one big name.

The Dodgers are also looking at how they prepare for the pitching they'll see in October. Gomes said the league's average fastball was about 94.5 mph last season, and hitting velocity will be a focus this winter. The front office is taking a fresh look at how it delivers scouting reports, and he expects the players who were swept to come back motivated.

"Knowing guys are hungry after the way things ended," he said.

Then there's Shohei Ohtani, who gets a normal offseason. Gomes said the Dodgers will bring Ohtani into the conversation about how to manage his two-way workload, with options like more days off as a hitter, so that he is at his best in October. "Shohei's open to putting the team in the best position to win," Gomes said. "He cares deeply about the Dodgers winning." Yoshinobu Yamamoto, he said, was as disappointed as anyone. "I don't know if he can be more motivated than he is," Gomes said.

None of this sounds like a team that's worried about what happens Dec. 1. It sounds like a team that's annoyed it didn't win.

"The goal is to be better than we were the year before," Gomes said, "and continuing to find ways to improve and get back to being a world champion."

Baseball may shut down in a few weeks. The rules may change. The schedule may shrink. But when the games come back, whenever that is, the Dodgers will field the most talented team in the sport. Again.

As Gomes put it, the goal is "a very long window and making sure that stays open."

The Brewers closed it this year. The Dodgers are already working on prying it back open.

articles.title: Brian Cashman accepts Pat Murphy's apology for saying 2023 Yankees had selfish culture
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS (AP) — Yankees general manager Brian Cashman accepted Pat Murphy's apology after the Milwaukee manager criticized New York's 2023 team for a selfis...
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS (AP) — Yankees general manager Brian Cashman accepted Pat Murphy's apology after the Milwaukee manager criticized New York's 2023 team for a selfish culture minutes after the Brewers won the World Series last month.

When first baseman Jake Bauers gave Murphy the ball from the last out of the Game 5 win over Tampa Bay on Oct. 28 , the manager used a profanity while referring to the Yankees.

Murphy made a reference to Bauers' likely big-money free agent contract this offseason and implored him to recall his time on the 2023 Yankees, who went 82-80 and failed to make the playoffs, and compare it with his success this year.

"You guys were all playing for yourself. Just remember, say, `This is the way we used to do it,'" Murphy said during the on-field celebration, a remark recorded in a video posted by Spectrum News 1 Wisconsin .

"He took the time on the greatest — within 12 hours, arguably some of the greatest times that he's had walking this planet Earth outside of the birth of his kids — to realize that he said something that he regretted, that he's caught on a live mike," Cashman said Tuesday at the general managers meetings. "He wanted to take the time, track us down over here at the lowly New York Yankees to make sure he would apologize for that, so that meant a lot to me."

Cashman said Murphy explained "how he kind of utilizes things — anything he can to motivate his players."

Murphy won the NL Manager of the Year award Tuesday night, becoming the first skipper in either league to earn the honor three seasons in a row.

New York was swept by Tampa Bay in an AL Division Series and has not won the World Series since its 26th title in 2009 .

"The Marlins beat us in the World Series and I remember they put our logo on the World Series ring, that they beat the Yankees," Cashman said. "We have a history of success that we're always trying to live up to."

Cashman said he understands the anger of the team's fan base at the end of each season without a title.

"Do I get upset? Initially, yeah. Do I get motivated? Absolutely, always," he said, surrounded by reporters. "I don't need anything to motivate me. I feel like our fans and you guys and girls keep us motivated enough. If that doesn't, I mean, we've got a cattle prod constantly stuck right where you don't want it non-stop with electrodes going. So that keeps you alive. But also when you take a step back, you've got to channel and recognize it's coming from a place of hope and love of wanting things to be better than they currently are."

Cashman, entering his 30th season in charge of baseball operations with the Yankees, said his new contract had been finalized but didn't reveal its length.

"Even though we've been there before, it hasn't been as timely as it needs to be, so I get it," he said of the title drought. "And the longer it goes, the louder it gets."

Yankees left-hander Max Fried had surgery to remove a bone spur from his pitching elbow.

"That was a late surgery added," Cashman said. "Six weeks of rest and rehab and then a throwing program starting sometime I think second week of December. Should be ready for spring training."

Fried, a three-time All-Star who turns 33 in January, was 5-5 with a 2.80 ERA in 20 starts. Because of what the team said was a left elbow bone bruise, he didn't pitch for the Yankees between May 15 and July 22, and between Aug. 13 and 29.

Cashman said he was surprised former All-Star catcher Jorge Posada said on a podcast with New York Post reporters that the team made him felt unwelcome.

"If any of our former guys want to engage, they know where to find us," Cashman said. "He is welcome. I obviously did have those conversations with him. ... Jorge wants us to be great. We want us to be great. And unfortunately we haven't been — we've been good but we haven't been great."

articles.title: Bath volleyball eyes historic regional title after semifinal sweep
articles.summary: The Bath volleyball team is chasing a historic regional title after sweeping Marlette in the Division 3 state tournament.
articles.body:
BATH — A year ago, Kyria Pairolero and the Bath volleyball team accomplished all it listed on its preseason goal sheet.

They won a tournament and also captured a district championship among other things during a successful 2025 season.

With a team full of returners, Bath has made it a point to accomplish more this year.

"We took every single one of those goals that we had last year and set them up a notch," Pairolero said. "It wasn't win a tournament, it was win three tournaments. It was like this kind of stuff."

The Bees have accomplished much of what they set out to do in what has turned out to be a special season that has included CMAC regular season and tournament titles and a district championship.

Bath has more it wants to achieve and took a step toward its bid to make history by sweeping Marlette in three sets by scores of 25-13, 25-17 and 25-22 in a Division 3 regional semifinal on its home floor Tuesday, Nov. 10.

The win sends the Bees into a regional final against Leslie on Thursday, Nov. 12.

"They are just a really highly motivated group of kids," Bath coach Madison Margraves-Beukema said. "They really are kind of chasing after the same goals. We've been working towards a long list of goals this year. One of them is to make history at our school. We've never had a regional championship at our school. They are just really, really motivated to try to do that. We're really glad to get to move on to the next day."

A year ago the Bees had their postseason run halted by Reese in a regional semifinal in what was their first appearance in the second stage of the MHSAA state tournament since 2020. Now after Tuesday's win Bath has matched the state tournament run made by the 2018 squad coached by Kristen McIntyre that reached the regional final before being eliminated.

Pairolero and teammates now want to have a different outcome than that group and aim to build on a special season that included the Bees not dropping a set in CMAC play through the regular season and postseason tournament. Bath also hasn't dropped a set yet in the state tournament and overcame a 22-19 deficit in the third set to wrap up its regional semifinal victory.

"Most of us are returning players so I feel like we all just kind of had a bone to pick," Pairolero said. "We wanted to get back to this place. That was one of our first goals. I know that was my goal. We really, really wanted to work hard and our goal was to stay undefeated at home so this is just another step."

Leslie reached the regional final with a sweep of Burton Atherton, winning each game by a 25-10 score.

articles.title: Cubs pitcher Ben Brown has neck surgery, likely won't resume throwing until midseason
articles.summary: LAS VEGAS (AP) — Chicago Cubs pitcher Ben Brown had neck surgery and likely won't resume throwing until midseason.Cubs general manager Carter Hawkins said th...
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS (AP) — Chicago Cubs pitcher Ben Brown had neck surgery and likely won't resume throwing until midseason.

Cubs general manager Carter Hawkins said the 27-year-old right-hander was operated on Monday in New York because of a stress fracture in his neck. Hawkins said a screw was implanted to improve healing

"He's walking around the streets of New York. He'll start throwing the ball after the new year, most likely midseason," Hawkins said Tuesday. "We've got to figure out where he is weeks from now to really understand how much we're going to be able to stick to that plan."

Brown didn't pitch after June 19 because of what the team said was a neck strain. He was 4-2 with a 1.85 ERA in eight starts and 12 relief appearances, striking out 65 and walking 19 in 68 innings.

Brown is 10-13 with a 4.15 ERA and two saves in 31 starts and 29 relief appearances over three major league seasons.

Chicago said the same condition bothered Brown in 2024.

articles.title: Jaguars-Ravens averages 13.96 million on Prime Video
articles.summary: When it comes to interpreting press releases regarding the audiences for sporting events, there's a rule of thumb.
articles.body:
When it comes to interpreting press releases regarding the audiences for sporting events, there's a rule of thumb.

The higher the number appears in the release, the better the company thinks the audience is. The lower the number appears in the release, the less impactful the figure is.

And if the number is really bad, there's no release at all.

For the Week 9 Thursday night game between the Jaguars and Ravens— which was destined to have a non-stellar audience thanks to the Ravens being down to their third-string quarterback — Prime Video led with the fact that the eight-game season-to-date average has outperformed last year's numbers.

The 33-10 win by the Jaguars, which Prime Video accurately called "lopsided" in the release, generated an average of 13.96 million viewers.

It nevertheless was, as Prime Video notes, a 13-percent bump over last year's Week 9 Thursday night game. And for good reason. The Week 9 Thursday night game in 2025 featured the Ravens at the Dolphins, a 28-6 Baltimore win.

Even with an audience of less than 14 million in the eighth TNF game of the season, the package is offering 17.15 million per week for 2026.

This week's game — Commanders at Giants — should do well, given that the Giants are both doing well and occupy the nation's top market. In Week 11, it's Colts at Texans. Which won't be great.

The following week, Prime Video has a potentially massive game on Black Friday between the currently 7-2 Broncos and 6-2 Steelers.

After that, it's Chiefs-Rams, Vikings-Patriots, 49ers-Chargers, Texans-Eagles (on Christmas Eve), and Ravens-Bengals.
