Kazakhstan's Bibisara Assaubayeva is the other woman in the 24-player field, with both facing a challenging examination in the days ahead.Carlsen sets the early pace with unbeaten blitz triumphWhile Vaishali supplied one of the evening's most interesting stories, Magnus Carlsen ensured the opening tournament belonged to him.The Norwegian world No. 1 won the nine-round blitz competition unbeaten, finishing with seven points out of nine to take the early lead in the inaugural Total Chess event.French Grandmaster Maxime Vachier-Lagrave finished second with 6.5 points, while Armenian-American Levon Aronian took third place with six.Carlsen sealed top spot by defeating Armenia's Haik Martirosyan with the black pieces in the final round. Vachier-Lagrave, meanwhile, could only manage a draw against Niemann, allowing the five-time classical world champion to finish clear at the top.The victory was more significant than just another addition to Carlsen's impressive collection of blitz titles. Under Total Chess's unusual competition rules, the opening tournament carries strategic importance beyond the standings.The finishing positions determine tiebreak priority during the group stage, influence knockout pairings and give higher-ranked players the first choice of colour in knockout blitz games. Carlsen has therefore secured a potentially valuable advantage before the main championship has even got underway.India's Arjun Erigaisi also threatened to challenge for the top position after producing impressive victories against Vachier-Lagrave and American GM Fabiano Caruana. However, his campaign suffered a setback in the final round when he lost to Aronian.Erigaisi finished on 5.5 points, alongside Alireza Firouzja, Caruana, Niemann and local favourite Richard Rapport. Rapport had earlier delivered one of the evening's biggest surprises by defeating world No. 3 Caruana in the opening round.Fast Classic format brings the real testThe competition now moves into its new Fast Classic format on Wednesday, with all 24 participants divided into four groups of six.The games will be played at a time control of 45 minutes plus 30 seconds per move. Unlike conventional scoring, a win will be worth three points, while a draw will earn each player one point.Carlsen headlines Group C, where he will face Dutch No. 1 Anish Giri, his former Russian rival Ian Nepomniachtchi, Shakhriyar Mamedyarov, Martirosyan and 17-year-old Abhimanyu Mishra.Group B features Caruana, India's R Praggnanandhaa, Vincent Keymer and Rapport.Vaishali and Assaubayeva will be in Group D, alongside Vachier-Lagrave, Erigaisi, Niemann and So. That makes it a particularly intriguing group, especially after Vaishali's opening-round victories against two of its established names.Only the four group winners will advance to the main championship knockout bracket, although all 24 players will continue competing for their final positions.The $650,000 event is being organised as a pilot for a proposed new world tour combining Fast Classic, rapid and blitz chess, with the ambition of establishing a comprehensive measure of excellence across formats.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: PT Usha's second-term ambitions at crossroads: What are her options in IOA presidential race?
articles.summary: New Delhi: The Indian Olympic Association's (IOA) presidential race took an unexpected turn on Monday, with current chief PT Usha facing her biggest
articles.body: New Delhi: The Indian Olympic Association's (IOA) presidential race took an unexpected turn on Monday, with current chief PT Usha facing her biggest electoral setback since taking charge of the organisation in December 2022.Usha, who became the first woman to head the IOA, finished fifth in the election for the women's Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) category on November 9. With four positions available, she missed out on a place in the newly elected group that will form part of the IOA General Assembly, dealing a significant blow to her prospects of securing another term.The result has also altered the power dynamics within the country's apex sports body ahead of the December 5 Executive Council elections, which will determine who leads Indian Olympic administration for the next four years.However, Usha's electoral defeat does not, by itself, settle the question of her future. The IOA Constitution, ratified on September 8, and the Election Bye-Laws provide a framework that leaves some room for an alternative route. Whether that route is available to Usha, and whether she intends to pursue it, are now central questions.What does Usha's SOMs defeat mean for her presidential ambitions?Usha was elected unopposed as IOA president on December 10, 2022, after securing a place among the Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit. The SOM category has traditionally provided a route for accomplished sportspersons to enter the IOA General Assembly and subsequently contest elections to the Executive Council.The latest election, however, did not go her way.In the six-way contest for four women's SOM positions, long jumper Anju Bobby George topped the poll with 53 votes, followed by former India women's hockey captain Rani Rampal (50), former archer Dola Banerjee (45) and badminton player Saina Nehwal (43). Usha secured 40 votes, finishing behind Saina, while former basketball player Anitha Pauldurai received six.The four men's positions had already been filled unopposed by Olympic medallists Gagan Narang, Yogeshwar Dutt and Vijender Singh, along with former table tennis player Kamlesh Mehta.The eight elected SOMs will form part of the General Assembly and will be eligible to vote in the December 5 elections. One male and one female representative from this category will also be elected to the Executive Council.For Usha, the immediate consequence is that she will no longer have the SOM route that helped her enter the IOA's electoral structure in 2022.But does that automatically rule her out of the presidential race? Not necessarily.Can PT Usha still find a way into the General Assembly?The IOA Constitution provides for membership of the General Assembly through multiple categories, including representatives of National Sports Federations (NSFs), the Athletes Commission, IOC members and the eight SOMs.Under the election notification issued on November 9, each eligible NSF has been asked to nominate two authorised representatives to the Electoral College — one male and one female.The notification lists 30 eligible National Sports Federations. Each federation's representatives will have one vote apiece in the Executive Council elections.This potentially offers Usha an alternative route into the General Assembly, provided a federation nominates her as one of its authorised representatives and she meets the prescribed eligibility conditions.There are, however, important qualifications.The notification makes it clear that an authorised representative must be a member of the concerned NSF, an Indian citizen, below 70 years of age and in good standing. The nomination must also be supported by the federation's authorisation and submitted within the stipulated deadline.Therefore, Usha cannot simply secure a nomination from any federation without meeting its membership requirements.The Athletics Federation of India (AFI) is an obvious organisation to watch in this context, given Usha's association with athletics. However, there is no confirmed indication that she will be among its two representatives.More importantly, entering the General Assembly and satisfying the specific eligibility requirements for the post of president are two related but distinct considerations.The new Constitution's eligibility provision for the President and Treasurer requires a candidate to be a Sportsperson of Outstanding Merit or to have previously served at least one full term as a member of the IOA Executive Council, or as president, secretary general or treasurer of an affiliated unit.Usha's tenure as IOA president began in December 2022. Whether her current Executive Council service will be treated as a completed full term at the relevant eligibility cut-off is a question that will need to be assessed under the Constitution and by the Electoral Officer.The Constitution also provides for a four-year term for office-bearers, a three-term ceiling and a cooling-off provision in the circumstances specified under its tenure rules.Thus, while an NSF nomination could potentially restore her place in the General Assembly, it should not be viewed as an automatic clearance for the presidential contest.There is another significant development.According to reports, PT Usha is not currently considering seeking nomination from an NSF to regain entry into the General Assembly. Nor is she contemplating approaching the courts to challenge the SOM election result. Instead, her immediate focus appears to be on seeking intervention from the International Olympic Committee (IOC).Usha takes electoral battle to IOC: What is her next move?In a confidential three-page complaint, addressed to IOC president Kirsty Coventry, Usha has sought an independent examination of the SOM election process.The complaint, accessed by TOI, raises concerns about alleged campaigning by incumbent Executive Council members, communications seeking confirmation of voters' participation and references to the Sports Ministry in messages concerning a secret-ballot election.Usha has also questioned the handling of four representations she claims to have submitted to Returning Officer Sanjay K. Srivastava during the electoral process.She has argued that the issue is not simply about her defeat, but about the conduct and oversight of the election itself.Her complaint reportedly asks the IOC to examine the alleged violations, ascertain whether any government or external influence was exerted and consider referring the matter to its relevant ethics and compliance mechanisms.She has also sought corrective measures to safeguard future IOA elections.The letter comes against the backdrop of India's ambitions to host the 2036 Olympic Games. Usha has argued that the IOA's independence, transparency and governance standards are important to the credibility of the Olympic movement.Sources in her camp have indicated that the immediate hope is for IOC intervention, alongside efforts to seek the Prime Minister's Office's intervention into the alleged irregularities.Key dates in the IOA presidential electionsWith the SOM elections concluded, the IOA has moved to the next phase of its Executive Council election process. Electoral Officer Sanjay K. Srivastava has formally announced December 5 as the date for the Executive Council elections.The immediate task is to constitute the Electoral College, which will elect the next president and other office-bearers.Under the notification, the 30 eligible NSFs have been asked to submit the names of their two authorised representatives between November 10 and November 12, by 3 pm.The provisional Electoral College is scheduled to be published on November 12. Objections can be submitted until 6 pm on November 13, followed by scrutiny and disposal of objections on November 14. The final Electoral Roll is scheduled for publication on November 15.The Electoral College will comprise:- Two authorised representatives from each of the 30 eligible National Sports Federations.- IOC member(s), each entitled to one vote.- Two representatives of the IOA Athletes Commission.- Eight elected Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit, comprising four men and four women.The eight SOMs, therefore, will have a role beyond simply occupying positions in the General Assembly. They will also be part of the body that elects the next IOA leadership.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Grand Slam of Darts: Tommy Morris set to light up tournament in Wolverhampton with dance moves to rival Dimitri van den Bergh
articles.summary: Remember the name! Tommy Morris became only the sixth non-Tour Card holder to win a ProTour title, and now he is ready to let loose his dance moves at the Grand Slam of Darts; you can watch the tournament in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22
articles.body:
Morris, from Dorset, goes by the moniker 'The Gun' - like real-life boxer Tommy Morrison, who co-starred alongside Sylvester Stallone in the 1990 film Rocky V as the Oklahoma boxer Tommy Gunn.

Both have something to prove! The 34-year-old has charisma, style, and some serious dance moves, and now he's set to leave Dimitri van den Bergh, Ricky Evans and Devon Petersen trailing in his shadow.

Morris has already made his mark by beating his idol Gary Anderson, Michael van Gerwen, Rob Cross and Michael Smith - all former world champions.

"It's just proving to people what I can do. This is not just a pub game for me now," Morris declared to Sky Sports .

"At the start of the year I got invited to the first Pro Tour and it became sort of a domino effect. I'm glad I'm finally getting the results because I've kept going and not giving up. It's going great at the minute. It really is."

Morris, who established himself on the MODUS Super Series, revealed he doesn't want to "burst the balloon" when he makes his grand appearance on the big stage in Wolverhampton.

He has been drawn in Group C alongside former World Cup winner Josh Rock and Dutchman Kevin Doets.

"I can dance, but I want to make it a bit of a surprise," he said. "I've got a party theme tune lined up. You're going to love it. I'll have a little shake, and we can have a good vibe. That's what dancing is about - just entertaining!

"I'm a bit of a jester. I'm the fun one in the room. I don't take things as seriously because that one game can make you give up. I want to keep going. I've learned that I need good energy around me.

"This is what is helping me progress. Good people, good vibes. And I'm looking forward to my walk-ons."

Morris officially qualified for the World Championship for the first time, finishing third in the PDC Challenge Tour, but he will also feature at the Players Championship Finals in Minehead, as well as in Wolverhampton.

Tournaments are coming thick and fast for Morris, who said: "I'm just going to take it in my stride. If it doesn't go well, I'm still very proud of what I've done, what I'm doing. This is not the end of me. This is a start. So, this is the new progression that I need to get used to the cameras, the bigger stages.

"I'm hoping this develops me better as a player. And if it doesn't, I'm still going to keep working at it, plugging away. But as of today, I'm very proud of what I've done and what I've achieved from the start of the year."

Morris, who suffers from tinnitus in his ear, made it to Players Championship 32 final in Den Bosch where he was beaten by Chris Dobey, but he kept believing in his ability and sealed the Players Championship 34 title in Leicester with an emotional victory over former world champion Luke Humphries - sealed via a 161 checkout.

"I got so emotional when I actually done it. And if I'm honest, that hasn't even sunk in. These little platforms and what I'm doing, they're not really hitting me," he admitted.

"I feel like when I've been at the Pro Tour now, I feel like I can compete with these guys all the time. Not just go down the pub and play Barry the Butcher."

"I do class myself at the minute as one of the best players on the planet right now."

Morris' dream is beyond winning the Wimborne Championship where he resides, but to claim a full-time tour card on the PDC circuit.

He has struck up an unlikely friendship with veteran player Mervyn King, whom he sees as his mentor.

"Merv is one of my best friends in darts right now. If not my best friend, he mentors me. He also calms me down because I'm really fiery and he's really mellow. So this is why we work.

"We don't get into going out to pubs, celebrating. We'll go back, put the TV on and watch Vera or Silent Witness. We're a bit boring.

"We've got fishing trips planned so we're into the same hobbies, which is a bonus for what we do on and off the oche."

Sky Sports remains the home of darts with the Grand Slam of Darts (November 14-22) and World Darts Championship (December 11-January 3) all live. Stream darts and more through NOW with no contract.

articles.title: Jacobo Ramón desvela el secreto del Como: “Esto tiene un autor que es Cesc Fàbregas”
articles.standfirst: El central cuenta en La Tribu de Radio MARCA cómo le convenció Fàbregas para fichar por el Como y por qué el vestuario está “a muerte con la idea del míster”.
articles.summary: El central cuenta en La Tribu de Radio MARCA cómo le convenció Fàbregas para fichar por el Como y por qué el vestuario está “a muerte con la idea del míster”.
articles.body: Jacobo Ramón tenía ocho años cuando llegó al Real Madrid y llevaba doce en el club cuando decidió salir para demostrar qué clase de central podía ser lejos de Valdebebas. Encontró su sitio en el Como de Cesc Fàbregas y ahora afronta su primera convocatoria con la selección española. Desde Las Rozas, el defensa repasa en La Tribu de Radio MARCA las críticas que recibió tras su estreno como titular en Butarque, la llamada de Fàbregas que le convenció para irse a Italia y el mensaje de Assane Diao con el que se enteró de que estaba en la lista de España. P. ¿Cómo recuerdas tu primer partido como titular con el Real Madrid, en Butarque? R. Estuve muy contento ese día. Lo recuerdo con muchísimo cariño, a pesar de cómo fue el partido y de lo que pasó. Fue mi debut como titular con el Madrid, algo con lo que llevaba soñando mucho tiempo. P. ¿Cómo llevaste las críticas tras aquel penalti? R. El Madrid es el club más exigente del mundo y sabía que después de ese partido iba a recibir algunas críticas. Con el apoyo de mi familia y de la gente que tengo cerca lo acabas llevando. Sabía que era un partido y luego tuve la oportunidad de salir para demostrar el jugador que era. P. Llegaste al Madrid con ocho años y pasaste doce en el club. ¿Fue difícil tomar la decisión de salir? R. Yo también sabía que había llegado mi momento. Es muy difícil estar en el primer equipo, la competencia es máxima y creo que tenía que demostrar fuera el jugador que era. Di el paso correcto en el momento justo y, de momento, me está saliendo bien. P. ¿Qué te sedujo del Como? R. El proyecto era muy ambicioso. El año pasado ya hicimos una temporada muy buena y conseguimos clasificarnos para la Champions. Y, por supuesto, Cesc. Me llamó, me contó su idea de juego y creo que encajaba perfectamente con el futbolista que soy. Tuve pocas dudas de que era el sitio adecuado para mí. P. ¿Te sorprendió que Cesc Fàbregas te conociera tan bien? R. Dani Guindos, su segundo entrenador, ya me había tenido en las categorías inferiores del Madrid. Imagino que me conocía un poco más gracias a él. Cesc también había visto algún partido mío y le encajaba en su esquema de juego. P. ¿Cuál es el secreto de este Como, capaz de marcar nueve goles en un partido? R. Fue un partido en el que nos salió todo. No creo que nos vuelva a pasar muy a menudo. El secreto es el equipo. Estamos todos muy comprometidos y a muerte con la idea del míster. Esto tiene un autor, que es Cesc. Está trabajando muy bien con nosotros y, de momento, le estamos respondiendo. P. ¿Qué le dirías a alguien que todavía no ha visto un partido del Como? R. Creo que tenemos una propuesta atractiva. Intentamos presionar muy arriba, recuperar el balón lo más arriba posible y jugar con la línea muy adelantada. Con el balón buscamos construir desde atrás y generar ocasiones cuando conseguimos salir de la presión del rival. P. ¿Cómo te enteraste de tu convocatoria con la selección española? R. Estaba tranquilo en casa y, de repente, me llamó Assane Diao gritando. Le pregunté qué pasaba y me dijo que mirara la foto que me había mandado. Era la lista de convocados. Al principio pensé que me estaba vacilando, pero miré la hora y era justo cuando salía la lista. Entonces dije que me lo iba a tener que creer. Me puse muy contento. P. ¿Te lo esperabas? R. Sabía que estaba en la prelista y que tenía alguna posibilidad, pero tampoco le di muchas vueltas. Para mí esto es un regalo. Si salía, bien, y si no, mi camino iba a seguir igual. Gracias a Dios, al final tengo esta oportunidad. P. ¿Cómo han sido tus primeras horas en la concentración? R. Hay jugadores a los que llevo viendo desde pequeño. A muchos los conocía sobre todo de verlos por la tele. Me han recibido muy bien y estoy muy agradecido. P. ¿Quién ha estado más pendiente de ti en la llegada? R. Un poco todos. Al principio soy algo tímido y me lo están poniendo muy fácil. Huijsen ha estado bastante pendiente de mí y Cubarsí se ha sentado conmigo en la mesa. En general, todos me han ayudado mucho. P. ¿Te imaginas compartiendo vestuario con Huijsen en el Real Madrid? R. No lo sé. Ahora mismo estoy centrado en el Como. Tenemos una temporada muy bonita por delante. Estamos en noviembre, prácticamente acabamos de empezar, y ya tenemos bastante con lo que tenemos en Italia. De verdad que no pienso en eso. P. ¿Te das cuenta al salir de que en el Castilla vivías en una burbuja? R. Sí, sin duda. Llegué muy pequeño al Madrid y te acostumbras al ambiente y a las instalaciones. Cuando sales te das cuenta de que incluso en el Castilla tienes más recursos que en muchos equipos de Primera División. P. ¿Cómo se afrontan los ataques en redes cuando acabas de debutar con el Real Madrid? R. Como futbolistas sabemos que estamos expuestos. En redes cualquiera puede escribir lo que quiera y encima te puedes enterar. Ahí es muy importante la mentalidad que tengas, que te afecte lo menos posible. La primera vez siempre te afecta más. El Madrid es el equipo más expuesto del mundo y, si no lo haces bien y los resultados no acompañan, sabes que te van a criticar. Lo importante es superarlo y que no te afecte de cara al futuro. P. ¿A ti te afectó lo que leíste después del partido de Leganés? R. La primera vez me sorprendió todo lo que me estaba llegando. Intenté superarlo rápido pensando que realmente no conocía a esa gente. Para mí lo importante era lo que pensaran dentro del Madrid y, sobre todo, el cariño de mi familia y mis amigos. P. ¿Qué le dirías a quien decide en 45 minutos que un canterano no vale para el Madrid? R. Cada uno puede tener su opinión, pero un futbolista no se demuestra en 45 minutos. Hay muchísimos factores que pueden determinar un partido, incluida la suerte. Si ese día el balón te da en la mano, es penalti y ya está. Los que llegan al primer equipo están muy preparados. Si están ahí es por algo. El nivel lo tienen. P. ¿En qué central te has mirado desde pequeño? R. En Sergio Ramos. Soy central, crecí en el Madrid y para nosotros era el referente. P. ¿Cuál es tu primer recuerdo de la selección española? R. El Mundial de 2010. Tenía cinco años, pero todavía recuerdo algo de aquel Mundial que ganamos. P. Luis Milla dijo que no le extrañaría ver a Cesc Fàbregas en el Real Madrid. ¿A ti te sorprendería que diera el salto a un gran banquillo? R. No sé si al Madrid o a cualquier otro equipo, pero a un gran banquillo desde luego que no. Es un pedazo de entrenador, lo está demostrando en el Como y seguro que tiene una carrera increíble por delante. P. ¿Eres de los que, si juegan el domingo, se ven tres o cuatro partidos el sábado? R. Sí, soy de esos. Me gusta mucho el fútbol y veo muchos partidos. P. ¿Cómo ves la pelea entre el Real Madrid, el Barcelona y el Atlético en LaLiga? R. Está bonita ahora mismo. Los tres están en un pañuelo y están dando un nivelazo. Cuanto más bonita esté la Liga, mejor para el espectador.

articles.title: Betis: pérdidas de 15 millones en 2025-2026 para ir a por 200 millones de negocio con la Champions
articles.standfirst: El club prevé elevar su negocio un 16% esta temporada, impulsado por el gran torneo europeo y líneas al alza como la de abonados y socios
articles.summary: El club prevé elevar su negocio un 16% esta temporada, impulsado por el gran torneo europeo y líneas al alza como la de abonados y socios
articles.body: El Real Betis ha vuelto a la Champions League. Veintiún años después de la última vez, el club de LaLiga EA Sports compite esta temporada en la máxima competición europea. Un éxito que ha requerido un esfuerzo extra por parte de la entidad, y eso en términos financieros supone, muchas veces, asumir pérdidas. En su caso, registró unos números rojos de 15,2 millones en 2025-2026, en contraposición a los 4,6 millones de beneficio de la temporada inmediatamente anterior. Sin embargo, el negocio del Betis sigue creciendo a un ritmo acelerado, con una facturación ordinaria récord de 162,9 millones, un 8% más interanual. Ahora el objetivo es acercarse a los 190 millones en 2026-2027, al margen de lo que adicionalmente puedan aportar las plusvalías por traspasos. Con ello, y con la vuelta a un renovado Benito Villamarín en el horizonte, el escenario a medio plazo pasa por superar los 200 millones y sin depender de los traspasos, como ya avanzó su CEO, Ramón Alarcón, en 2Playbook hace cuatro años. “El club ha decidido llevar a cabo una inversión, asumir esta pasada temporada unas pérdidas controladas y tener una plantilla deportiva competitiva”, explica hoy Cristina Lafuente, directora financiera del Real Betis, en conversación con este medio. El plan del club es poder “recuperar esa inversión en dos o tres años”, avanza la ejecutiva, quien remarca la importancia de esta apuesta en plantilla deportiva para conseguir hitos como la clasificación para la Champions League. El último año, la masa salarial alcanzó los 128,4 millones de euros entre salarios deportivos y amortizaciones por fichajes, un 16% más que el curso anterior. “Esas inversiones en jugadores se trasladan a cuenta de resultados, y por eso el incremento en esta parcela”, apunta. Asimismo, “otra decisión que adoptó el club fue no vender determinados jugadores este verano con el objetivo de llegar lejos deportivamente”. Es decir: el Betis pudo haber rebajado las pérdidas o mantenerse en beneficios con una gran venta, pero rechazó optar por esta vía. A cierre de curso, el valor de la plantilla en libros ascendía a 99,8 millones de euros. Para Lafuente, la clave del futuro a corto y medio plazo de las finanzas del club pasa por “seguir trabajando sobre los ingresos operativos del club”. Además de esto, el club mantiene su senda de realizar ventas de futbolistas cada verano. Desde la pandemia, el Betis ha generado 219,6 millones de euros en plusvalías por traspasos, según datos extraídos de Intelligence 2P, la unidad de estrategia e inteligencia de mercado de 2Playbook. La media anual son 31,4 millones. Esta última temporada, el plan de retención de sus principales activos deportivos para competir en Champions, hizo que el beneficio por esta vía cayera casi un 60%, hasta 23,4 millones de euros. “En la mayoría de clubes, las plusvalías por traspasos ya son ingresos recurrentes”, reconoce Lafuente. En el equipo verdiblanco, “todavía tenemos que hacer plusvalías, pero uno de nuestros objetivos es reducir esa dependencia de los traspasos”. En este punto, la ejecutiva destaca el trabajo de cantera del Real Betis. Con la nueva ciudad deportiva, inaugurada hace justo tres años, el club confía en ir sumando jugadores de su fútbol base en el primer equipo. “Para nosotros es estratégica la cantera”, asegura la directora financiera del club andaluz. El Nuevo Benito Villamarín es una piedra angular del crecimiento futuro de las finanzas béticas, y el traslado a La Cartuja -con el consiguiente aumento del aforo- avala ese plan. Con vistas a inaugurarse en 2029, la última actualización de costes del renovado recinto se cifraba en 262 millones de euros. El Plan Impulso -y los fondos de CVC- sólo cubrirá un 6% de la financiación. En este punto, Lafuente apunta que el mayor reto financiero es el actual, mientras se va pagando y asumiendo los costes de la obra y aún no se activan los ingresos. Después llegará el reto operativo, al que la ejecutiva le da gran importancia. La realidad es que el negocio del nuevo estadio debería tener un doble beneficio: impulsar los ingresos del club y, al mismo tiempo, rebajar la necesidad de negociar salidas de futbolistas para cubrir los presupuestos al alza que proyectará la entidad a medio plazo si se mantiene en Europa. Por ahora, la masa social responde y hace creer en el potencial del nuevo estadio. En La Cartuja, con mayor capacidad que el Villamarín, hay sold out en muchos partidos y la cifra de abonados no deja de crecer. En 2025-2026, el Betis recaudó 28,3 millones por socios y abonados, un 30% más interanual y un nuevo récord. Es el doble respecto a antes de la pandemia. Por competiciones y matchday –venta de entradas, principalmente- se anotó 11,4 millones, un 90% más interanual. Mientras, la televisión rozó los 98 millones de euros, un 14% más respecto a 2024-2025, gracias a su trayectoria en Europa League y la clasificación a Champions en LaLiga. Finalmente, la pata comercial sufrió un ajuste del 31%, pero se mantuvo por encima de los 25 millones. En la última temporada y la mitad de la presente, el club ha sumado casi una decena de nuevos patrocinadores. Entre ellos, marcas nuevas en LaLiga como Monster, internacionales como Prima, Maurice Lacroix o la más reciente, Drôle de Monsieur, y otras emergentes como la fintech española Ebury. En la equipación se mantiene Gree, main sponsor, y Hummel, socio técnico, con quien renovó hasta 2035 la temporada pasada. Este acuerdo es estratégico para la entidad, ya que le permite entrar de lleno en la producción de moda deportiva. En cuanto al gasto, junto a la ya anteriormente mencionada masa salarial, cabe destacar los 114 millones invertidos en personal. En salarios deportivos, el Betis destinó 95,2 millones en 2025-2026, un 9% más, y las amortizaciones por fichajes aumentaron en 10 millones, hasta 33,2 millones de euros. En balance, el patrimonio neto se mantiene negativo, en 54 millones, pero con el business plan que tiene en marcha el Betis confía en darle vuelta y generar fondos propios positivos a medio plazo. Ahí, de nuevo, el regreso al Benito Villamarín y la activación de nuevos ingresos tendrá un papel fundamental. Además, la deuda financiera neta se mantiene estable en algo más de 250 millones de euros. Y si el club requiriera de fondos, el Betis estaría bien posicionado en este pujante contexto de inversión internacional del fútbol español. “Estos fondos conocen perfectamente el sector y las situaciones financieras de los clubes. Saben identificar perfectamente aquellos clubes cuyas pérdidas suponen un problema, y aquellos clubes que son una inversión”, apostilla Lafuente.

Sherrock, who reached the third round of the PDC World Darts Championship in 2020, claimed the £501,000 jackpot when she defeated 'The Nuke' in a one-leg shoot-out during 'Beat Luke Littler' on October 30.

Littler told the Press Association , ahead of his Grand Slam of Darts defence live on Sky Sports from Saturday : "Before I saw the line-up, I thought it was just pub players. Whereas obviously when the line-up came out, I probably knew just over half of them.

"There aren't many people who could say they've got their own show and I've had my own show on Netflix, which is just still bonkers to me.

Ezri Konsa is set to miss England's opening game of this international break against Croatia after being ruled out of the fixture. His absence is a setback for the national team, particularly given the defender's importance and the confidence Thomas Tuchel has shown in him.

The defender is regarded as one of the best players in his position in the country and has earned Tuchel's trust. The German manager regularly includes him in his squad, demonstrating the importance he places on having Konsa available for international duty.

He has also been an important performer for Arsenal since joining the Gunners in the summer from Aston Villa . His contributions have made him one of the club's key players at the Emirates, and his continued development has been encouraging.

Konsa's absence creates a selection change

Arsenal will be proud to see him representing his country, but his involvement against Croatia will have to wait. ESPN reports that Konsa will miss the match, with England already making arrangements to bring in a replacement for the defender.

According to the report, Tuchel has called up James Hill of Bournemouth to replace Konsa in the squad. The decision provides England with another defensive option ahead of their opening fixture of the international break.

However, Konsa has not been sent home from the England camp, leaving open the possibility that he could still feature later in the window.

England could still have Konsa available

Although Konsa is definitely unavailable for the Croatia match, there remains a possibility that he could recover in time for England's next fixture against Spain. His situation will therefore be worth monitoring as the international break progresses.

Keeping him in the squad suggests that England are not ruling out his involvement in the second match. However, his availability will depend on his recovery and whether he is ready to return to action.

The two fixtures against Croatia and Spain are the Nations League matches England will contest during this international break. Tuchel and his players will be keen to secure victories in both games, making squad availability particularly important as they prepare for the challenges ahead.

articles.title: Amad: Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival will help United star realise his true potential
articles.summary: Amad is in his sixth year at Manchester United and it is safe to say that he has not lived up to expectations. The Ivorian arrived at Old Trafford in January...
articles.body:
Amad is in his sixth year at Manchester United and it is safe to say that he has not lived up to expectations. The Ivorian arrived at Old Trafford in January 2021 from Atalanta as one of the most exciting teenage forwards in the world.

It appeared that the Red Devils had secured a future superstar who could become the backbone of the attack. For a club that had struggled to impress in the transfer market, it certainly looked like a coup.

Unfortunately, Amad has shown extended flashes of brilliance but is yet to truly blow everyone away.

Amad had a brief taste of English football in his first six months before he was loaned to Rangers in the summer of 2022. A year later, he secured a temporary deal to Sunderland, where he finally exploded.

The Ivorian was a revelation with the Black Cats, registering 14 goals and four assists in 42 appearances across all competitions. Sunderland wanted him back the following season, but Amad ended up staying.

He initially struggled for game time under Erik ten Hag before becoming a regular under Ruben Amorim, scoring 10 goals and registering 11 assists. While he has been heavily involved under Michael Carrick as well, the player has yet to reach the heights expected of him.

Amad is yet to score a goal since Carrick's arrival as Amorim's replacement. Last season, the Ivorian was heavily involved under the Englishman, operating mostly in the right-forward role.

He missed the start of the current campaign with a knock and has started the last five games in the Premier League. Unfortunately, in his 25 games under Carrick, Amad has failed to find the back of the net, managing just two assists.

Recent reports suggest that the English manager is on the brink of losing his job, with Mauricio Pochettino leading the race to become the next United manager. The Argentine's potential arrival, however, could turn out to be good news for the Ivorian.

Amad suits Pochettino's attacking system

Pochettino likes his wide forwards to tuck inwards, which brings the full-backs into play. He has previously used similar tactics with Christian Eriksen and Dele Alli at Tottenham Hotspur and Neymar and Kylian Mbappé at Paris Saint-Germain (PSG).

Amad likes attacking diagonally from the right while coming onto his left foot, which also allows full-backs to overlap. The Ivorian is a willing runner with impressive control in tight spaces and the ability to see a pass.

He is blessed with blistering pace and has good dribbling ability. Under Pochettino, he could regularly receive the ball in the opposition half, combine with Bruno Fernandes and carry the ball into the penalty box to make an impact.

Amad's pressing also suits Pochettino's tactics

Amad has all the technical attributes to thrive in Pochettino's attacking system, but his work ethic could also make him invaluable for the Argentine.

Pochettino's tactics demand a lot of pressing from the forwards, who are expected to spring into action as soon as possession is lost and close passing lanes. Winning the ball higher up the pitch creates opportunities, effectively turning defence into a form of attack.

Amad's willingness to track back and press the opposition makes him perfect for the job, so he would not have to make too much of an adjustment under the Argentine manager.

For all of Amad's qualities, his poor record in front of goal remains a concern for fans. The 24-year-old has managed just 16 goals and 17 assists in 105 appearances for United to date, which do not justify his talent.

This is one area Pochettino can help him improve, having previously done so with Alli and Eriksen. The presence of Bryan Mbeumo could pose a problem for the Ivorian, but perhaps the competition could help him hit a higher gear as well.

Amad's skills on the ball and tenacity off it could make him a perfect fit in Pochettino's high-intensity football. The Argentine is known to mix aggressive pressing with fast attacking transitions, which is exactly how the Ivorian likes to play.

Pochettino's potential arrival, as such, could be just the boost Amad needs to reach his potential at Old Trafford. The Argentine could help the Ivorian transition from a speedy winger to a goalscoring threat and eventually, one of United's most influential players.

articles.title: Verstappen and Hadjar call out Pirelli's wet tyres ahead of cold Las Vegas
articles.summary: Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar were among the group of Formula 1 drivers calling on Pirelli to improve its wet-weather tyres after the Sao Paulo Grand Prix....
articles.body:
Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar were among the group of Formula 1 drivers calling on Pirelli to improve its wet-weather tyres after the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

Interlagos was the first weekend of 2026 to be properly affected by rain. Aquaplaning and a narrow operating window made conditions more dangerous than the drivers had expected. Pirelli has responded that its tyres did what they were supposed to do.

Verstappen says cold wet tyres feel 'like a rock'

Verstappen climbed from 21st on the grid to finish second behind race winner Norris. After the race, he was critical of both the intermediate and the extreme-wet compounds. "I think it's mainly that the working range is a bit too small," the Red Bull driver said. "When they're hot, it's okay, but when they're cold, they're really like a rock."

The Dutchman wants a wider operating window, so drivers are not trying to build up grip while also coping with poor visibility and standing water. "That's something that we need to try and work on, to generate a bigger working range on the Extreme Wet and the Inter," he added.

Hadjar was even more direct. He qualified fifth on Saturday and went on to take his third podium of the season on Sunday. "I think [on Saturday], running an Extreme Wet compound, I didn't think there was a crazy amount of water on the track, and yet to me it felt like there was too much aquaplaning considering the conditions.

"For me, it also seems like you have to wait a while to put the Inter on. It's like you can run it once there's no more standing water and you can go at it. So, in a way, I feel like the compounds are a bit stiffer, harder than they used to be. I think we would all have a bit more fun with more grip, and I think there were times in qualifying yesterday where the very first three laps in Q1 were quite dangerous."

Norris believes the next race could show the problem most clearly. Low temperatures in Las Vegas already make tyre warm-up difficult, even in the dry.

"I think the scary times are if you go to Vegas and you can't get any tyre temperature. You need a much better tyre than what we have here because that's going to be horrible."

Pirelli insists its tyres met expectations

Pirelli rejected the drivers' view of the weekend. "Overall, both the Intermediate and the Soft performed in line with expectations, offering teams several strategic options in a race defined by uncertainty over the conditions," motorsport director Dario Marrafuschi said.

articles.body:
The high school basketball season has arrived, and several games have already tipped off.

Now, its time for the 910Preps Fans to choose the 910Preps Preseason Player of the Year.

Fayetteville Academy is three games in and holds a 1-2 record, while Cumberland Prep is 2-1 on the young season.

A season ago, Douglas Byrd's Marcus "MJ" McDuffie won the District 4 Player of the Year after leading the Eagles, and Jackson Williams won Eastern Sandhills Player of the Year.

Voting is now open for the 910Preps Fans' Choice Preseason Boys' Basketball Player of the Year, and 11 nominees are on the ballot.

Vote as often as you like. The poll closes on Wednesday, Nov. 18 at 9 a.m.

Parents , coaches, and athletic directors: When casting your vote, send a headshot photo of your athlete to jfmoore@usatodayco.com to include in the winner's article.

Christian Baynes, senior, Fayetteville Academy — Baynes is arguably the best all-around player in Cumberland County coming into the season. Last season, he earned 9.8 points, 5.8 rebounds, and 4.3 assists per game. This season, he'll likely become the primary ball-handler, and his numbers should double.

Jayvon Foster, senior, Seventy-First — Foster is one of the high-volume scorers in the Fayetteville area and can score at all three levels of the court. In his junior year, he averaged 15.5 points, 2.8 rebounds, 2.7 assists, and two steals per game.

Jaylen Mason, sophomore, E.E. Smith — Mason is a new transfer from Fayetteville Academy with one of the highest ceilings in the Fayetteville area and is regarded as the next player to blow up. In seven games with the Eagles' senior-heavy roster, he averaged 5.7 points and two assists. The 6-foot-4 wing holds offers from Hampton, George Mason, and Tennessee State.

Malachi McDuffie, junior, Douglas Byrd — While Malachi is the shortest player on the list at 5-foot-9, Byrd's point guard has one of the biggest motors in the area. He helped his brother, MJ lead Byrd to the playoffs and averaged 11.2 points, 3.5 assists, 3.3 rebounds, and 2.5 steals per game.

MJ McDuffie, junior, Douglas Byrd — McDuffie returns as one of the best bigs in the Fayetteville area. After helping Douglas Byrd return to relevance a season ago, he finished the season with an 18-8 record, the Eastern Sandhills Conference Player of the Year award, and averaged 18.8 points, 9.5 rebounds, and 1.3 blocks per game while shooting 64% from the field.

DeRyian Mitchell, junior, Cumberland Prep — Mitchell is a high-flying, high-volume scoring point guard, one of the best in the area, and has an extremely high ceiling. He embraces a bigger role at Cumberland Prep after departing from Jack Britt, where he averaged 15.3 points, 4.9 rebounds, 3.6 assists, and 2.6 steals.

Ja'Von Motta, senior, Trinity Christian — Motta had a productive junior season as the Crusaders' newcomer. The 6-foot-1 guard averaged 17.1 points, 4.6 rebounds, 2.4 assists, and 2.2 steals in 32 games.

Jeremiah Murchison, sophomore, Northwood Temple — Murchison is one of the most athletic guards in the area, and can score with the best of them, showcasing an array of 40-point performances last season at KSR. As a freshman, he averaged 21.3 points per game.

Nick Smith, junior, E.E. Smith — Nick Smith, the lefty point guard, is one of the craftiest ball handlers in Cumberland County, and his sophomore year put the state on notice. He was a driving force in the Golden Bulls' regional finals run and averaged 14.8 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 3.3 steals per game.

Bryce West, senior, Fayetteville Academy — West is undoubtedly the best shooter in Fayetteville and potentially in the state. Last season at Freedom Christian, Bryce averaged 26.9 points for No. 15 in the state, 5.7 rebounds, 3.5 assists, and made 128 3-point field goals for No. 1 in the state and 17th nationally.

Jackson Williams, senior, E.E. Smith — Williams had an exciting junior season, and his summer was even better. The combo guard has one of the highest on-court IQs in the city, led the Golden Bulls to the NCHSAA 6A East regional finals, earned first-team all-conference honors in the Eastern Sandhills, and gained offers from Pitt Community College and Johnson & Wales.

articles.title: Jamichael Stillwell powers Texas Tech basketball to historic win over Illinois in debut
articles.summary: Days after receiving a temporary restraining order to be eligible to play, Jamichael Stillwell made the most of his Texas Tech basketball debut.
articles.body:
Brad Underwood didn't need any film on Jamichael Stillwell with the Texas Tech basketball team to know what he brought to the table.

Days after receiving a temporary restraining order from a Lubbock judge, Stillwell made his Red Raider debut, stepping onto the United Supermarkets Arena floor before the first media timeout. A newcomer who Tech fans had never seen play in person (his lone game against Tech while at UCF came in Orlando), Stillwell was greeted to raucous cheers from every corner of the sold-out building.

"The fans love me," Stillwell said, "and I love y'all back."

Underwood knew the impact Stillwell could have, saying after the game the Atlanta native's penchant for grabbing offensive rebounds was notable in Illinois' scout work on the 6-foot-8 big man.

After the 16th-ranked Red Raiders claimed an 84-78 win over third-ranked Illinois — the highest-ranked nonconference opponent at home in Tech history — Underwood looked at the stat sheet and saw Stillwell's final damage: 11 points and 13 rebounds, six of them on the offensive glass.

"He literally, physically whipped our butt," Underwood said. "Give him credit. It's a pretty good first game."

Grant McCasland has been excited at the prospect of having Stillwell on the floor with this year's team. His first game as a Red Raider showed the reasons why.

Rebounding against a much taller and physical Fighting Illini frontcourt. Operating the pick-and-roll with Cruz Davis (game-high 20 points and five assists). Being in the right position more often than not defensively, even switching off onto guards along the perimeter as Texas Tech looked to put the game away.

"Jamichael Stillwell's a winner," McCasland said. "I mean, his physicality index is 100. He's amazing at putting his body in the middle of it consistently, and his belief in our team and his command. ... His presence alone in a game like that, you could, it just felt like he settled us, just going up and making free throws."

Stillwell has been practicing with the Red Raiders since joining the team in the late summer, initially on a temporary injunction in the state of Georgia. The NCAA earned a stay in that case, so Stillwell dropped out and refiled in Lubbock County last week, being granted a TRO from Judge John Grace, the same judge who awarded Donovan Atwell (13 points, five steals) his temporary injunction in October.

Being around the team this whole time, Stillwell said, made jumping in for his first game action easier.

"It really started off the court," Stillwell said. "Just with the chemistry, we always got that chemistry, and in practice, we just keep the same chemistry. I'm kind of easy to play with, so it wasn't hard."

Davis agreed with Stillwell's assessment of himself. He's easier to play with than most, and offers Texas Tech the ability to clamp down on defense like the team did in the closing minutes to put the game away.

"We all bring something different to the team, and having him back, he helped us out a lot," Davis said. "His first game back, gave us a double-double. He's able to make free throws, defend, rebound, I mean, he's easy wto play with in the pick-and-roll. Having him and everybody else — Don hit threes and stuff, so it just helped us out."

Positive as Stillwell's impact was, and for how historic the win over the Illini will be for years to come, McCasland doesn't think the team has lost sight of the ultimate goal.

articles.title: CFP committee explains Indiana football’s significant rankings drop
articles.summary: Why Indiana football was a victim of bad timing in latest set of CFP rankings.
articles.body:
BLOOMINGTON — Indiana football's five-spot drop in the latest set of CFP rankings rivaled Miami's fall out of the top spot and Kentucky's slide out of the top 10.

The No. 9 Hoosiers (8-1, 5-1 Big Ten) sat idle last weekend while the other teams played and lost.

After ESPN's weekly CFP rankings show, Hunter Yurachek, the chair of the selection committee, offered a window into the group's thinking.

"When the teams around you lose in the rankings and win big games, it affects where you land," Yurachek said on a conference call with reporters. "Even in the week you didn't lose or in some cases like Indiana didn't play, those are some of the toughest conversations in the room and why we saw such significant movement."

Best photos from Big Ten's Indiana Hoosiers versus Minnesota football

Indiana football's CFP resume takes a beating during off week

During the CFP committee's weekly meetings, they don't use their previous rankings as a jumping off point . The group starts from scratch and re-evaluate the entire field to take a "snapshot" of where things stand, as Yurachek described it on Tuesday night.

When the committee started deliberations at the Gaylord Texan Resort & Convention Center this week, Indiana's resume didn't hold up as well against like-competition.

"Indiana was probably the victim of having a bye week at the wrong time," Yurachek said.

Yurachek pointed to a slate of games last weekend that featured seven matchups among teams ranked in the top 25.

"Some of those big wins occurred right around where they were, starting with Notre Dame's big win over Miami," Yurachek said.

Notre Dame leapfrogged the Hoosiers in the latest rankings along with Alabama, Tennessee, Texas and UCLA. The Bruins were the only team that didn't play a ranked opponent, but their 34-20 win over Minnesota gave the committee a direct point of comparison to Indiana.

"UCLA went on the road and beat a Minnesota team, a Minnesota team that had gone to Indiana the week prior," Yurachek said. "Indiana needed a 60-yard field goal as time expired to send that game into overtime and win that game."

The other results in the Big Ten didn't help the Hoosiers either.

"Every team that Indiana played, had played to date in the Big Ten, they all lost," Yurachek said. "They had six losses that went against their record strength as well as their strength of schedule."

Indiana football's offensive struggles becoming CFP discussion point

Indiana's uncertainty at quarterback didn't have a direct impact on its ranking — Cignetti declined to name a starter for Saturday's game against USC — but the team's overall offensive struggles did.

Through the first five weeks of the season, the Hoosiers averaged 44.2 points and 489.6 total yards per game. Those numbers plummeted in recent weeks with the offense averaging 17.8 points and 332 total yards over the last four games.

During that stretch, Indiana has also struggled in the red zone (36.3% touchdown percentage) and turnovers (five).

"The quarterback play in general, the offensive play in general," Yurachek said. "Is a discussion point there for Indiana."

While IU's offensive metrics aren't standing out the same way they did in 2024 and 2025, the defense hasn't given up its crown and helped balance out some of the negatives on the team's resume.

"They're a dominant defensive team," Yurachek said. "One of the best, if not the best, defensive teams statistically in the country. They have won games because of their defense, not because of their offense. That is a point of discussion in the room when we are comparing them to other teams."

Michael Niziolek is the Indiana beat reporter for The Bloomington Herald-Times. You can follow him on X @michaelniziolek .

articles.title: Cross Country: Peoria Notre Dame high school coach Dan Gray earns hall of fame nod
articles.summary: Peoria Notre Dame coach Dan Gray is joining the Illinois Track and Cross Country Coaches Association Hall of Fame.
articles.body:
The Peoria Notre Dame cross country coach was announced as a member of the 2027 Illinois Track and Cross Country Coaches Association Hall of Fame class. Gray has been coaching cross country and track & field for almost 40 years, spending the majority of the time at PND.

"When I took at the other names are in that hall of fame, it doesn't feel like my name should be mentioned with other people," Gray told the Journal Star. "So many of those guys and women are legendary, and I feel like I have just been around for 40 yards — whatever it is, it is a nice honor."

He has served as both the Irish boys and girls cross country coach since 2014. Gray has also had a hand in four state champions: Caitlin Comfort (2006 Class AA cross country), C.J. Elward (2009-10 Class 2A 3200-meter run) and Maryjeanne Gilbert (2014-15 Class 2A cross country).

His coaching also helped the Irish claim a 2010 Class 2A cross country state championship and a 2007 Class 2A state runner-up finish.

"Some coaches show a clear skill at being able to excel at developing girls or boys," the ITCCCA said in its release . "Dan can do both and it's a testament to his ability to connect, build, trust, motivate, and get results."

Gray, who spent 10 seasons as the PND boys track & field coach, was won four boys cross country regional titles along with a 2023 Class 1A girls cross country third-place finish to go with four regionals and two sectionals. The Irish won girls regional and sectional titles during the 2026 cross country season.

This also marks the 50th anniversary of the ITCCCA Hall of Fame.

articles.title: Buffalo vs Ball State Prediction: Can the Cardinals Ruins the Bulls' MAC Hopes?
articles.summary: Buffalo is knee-deep in the MAC title chase, but Ball State has just enough pop to shake things up. Here's the CFN game preview and prediction.
articles.body:
All of a sudden, the MAC race took a huge turn with Miami University handing Ohio its first loss of the season on Tuesday night with a 34-17 win. Going into Wednesday, four MAC teams have one loss, and Buffalo is one of them. The Bulls have won four straight after a loss to Western Michigan, but they beat both Toledo and Miami University, both on the road. They still need some help, but they'll be knee-deep in the mix if they win out. Ball State isn't technically out of it at 2-3 in the conference, but it needs to go on a run, and the rest of the MAC has to melt down. The offense has picked it up over the last few weeks, and now its job is to throw a wrench into Buffalo's plans.

Buffalo hosts Central Michigan next and closes out at Akron.

Ball State goes to Ohio and finishes with Central Michigan.

Buffalo won 51-48 in the last meeting in 2024, but the Cardinals won two of the last three, including the 202 MAC Championship.

Date: Wednesday, November 11, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: ESPN2 Location: Scheumann Stadium, Muncie, IN – Week 11 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Bowl & CFP Projections | Top 25

The Bulls have been able to adapt and adjust on the fly. The running game rumbled in wins over UMass and Bowling Green, and the passing attack took over against Miami University. But it's mostly about the ground game. When it runs for over 150 yards, it's 5-0. Ball State's defense has plenty of problems, giving up over 150 yards in seven of its nine games, going 1-6.

Ball State has to take the fight to the Bulls right away. Buffalo thrives on takeaways, but Ball State doesn't turn the ball over, giving it up just eight times, with two turnovers in a win over Stony Brook and two in the overtime loss to UMass – the Cardinals don't beat themselves. Buffalo has chilled out on turnovers a little bit, but it gives the ball away with two or more giveaways five times, and Ball State has to capitalize on all of them.

Buffalo vs Ball State Prediction, Betting Lines

Neither team is all that consistent, but both have fun offenses that can open it up from time to time. The difference is that Ball State is far, far more effective at home. The Cardinals are 1-5 on the road, and even in a loss, the attack worked well against Toledo. They'll move the ball, but the defense won't come through in the second half as UB overcomes a slew of mistakes to finally start to pull away late. It'll grind away on the ground.

articles.title: Why Lyon didn’t approach Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage
articles.summary: Pierre Sage would have been a popular appointment at Olympique Lyonnais. The Frenchman, a boyhood fan of the club, has previously said that he has unfinished...
articles.body:
Pierre Sage would have been a popular appointment at Olympique Lyonnais. The Frenchman, a boyhood fan of the club, has previously said that he has unfinished business at the club, having left in early 2025 to be replaced by Paulo Fonseca.

Fonseca left OL last week in order to join his boyhood club, Sporting CP. Whilst Lyon did not want to lose the Portuguese manager, they didn't want to stand in his way.

The vacancy opened up the possiblity of Sage returning to the club, but it was instead Carlos Vicens, out of work since leaving SC Braga in October, who was appointed. Speaking at his unveiling, sporting director Matthieu Louis-Jean explained why the club did not move to bring back Sage.

Sage a priority target for Lens' president

"Pierre is under contract at Crystal Palace, so that wasn't an option. We worked on a list of manages with specific characteristics and Carlos matched perfectly," he said on Tuesday.

Of course, Sage may not be under contract at Crystal Palace for too much longer. He is expected to be relieved of his duties. A return to RC Lens, who he left to move to Selhurst Park over the summer, has been touted. In any case, he is the priority target for owner and president Joseph Oughourlian, L'Équipe understands.
